decls.name: blkDesign_step1
decls.docstring:
§9.7, Case 3a, step 1.  *"Apply the Design lemma to `H`, viewed as a `d₁`-ary
relational structure.  (Multiplicative cost `n₂^{d₁}`.)"*  (Version 2.5, lines 4277–4280.)

The Design Lemma is applied at the rank `N = d'` (`Babai.BlkCaseObj.d'`), to the
hypergraph on the blocks that `Babai.BlkDesignSetup.func` makes a functor of the input into
`Babai.DesignInputs (Set Ω) N (3/4)` — the admissible inputs of Theorem 8.1.2, whose three
hypotheses are checked in `Babai.BlkCaseObj.designObj` for Case 3a and in
`Babai.BlkCaseObj.skelDesignObj` for Case 3b.  What is found is one
*version* of the Design Lemma's answer, at the multiplicative cost of that answer, which is
`|V₂|^N = n₂^{d'}`.

The outcome category is the category of versions of `Babai.NormalRed.comap`, whose objects
carry the input as well; that is what lets step 2 use `V₁`, `α` and `n₂` of the input.

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Theorem 8.1.2 (Design lemma) (PDF p. 65) — §9.7, Case 3a, step 1.  *"Apply the Design lemma to `H`, viewed as a `d₁`-ary relational structure.  (Multiplicative cost `n₂^{d₁}`.)"*  (Version 2.5, lines 4277–4280.)

decls.name: blkDesign_step2
decls.docstring:
§9.7, **Cases 3a1 and 3a2**, the two sub-cases of Case 3a.  (Version 2.5,
lines 4281–4294.)

*"Case 3a1.  The Design lemma returns a canonical colored `3/4`-partition of `V₂`.  Apply
Cor. ??.  Significant progress is made in time, polynomial in `n₁`, namely, `n₂` is reduced
to `≤ 3n₂/4`.  If a multiplicative cost of `m` is incurred, the progress is more
significant: `n₂` is reduced to `≤ n₂/m` (`2 ≤ m ≤ n₂/2`).*

*Case 3a2.  The Design lemma returns a UPCC `Y` canonically embedded on a subset `W ⊆ V₂`
with `|W| ≥ (3/4)n₂`.  Apply Reduce-Part2-by-Color to the partition `(W, V₂ ∖ W)`.  If the
procedure selects `V₂ ∖ W`, significant progress (`n₂` reduced to `≤ n₂/4`).  If it selects
`W`, go to Sec. 9.8.  Let `U ⊆ V₂` be the part selected, and `(X₂)_new` the homogeneous
coherent configuration obtained on `U`.  If `(X₂)_new` is a UPCC, exit, significant
progress.  If `(X₂)_new` is not a UPCC, i. e., it has rank 2, then `U` was a clique in `Y`
and therefore `|U| ≤ |W|/2 ≤ n₂/2` by Prop. 2.4.11, a significant reduction of `|V₂|."*

The hypothesis is the conclusion of the Design Lemma at a version: `G'` is the canonical
embedding that reads the answer off a version, and `hgood` says that the answer is an
outcome of Theorem 8.1.2 for the threshold `3/4` on `V₂` — *"a canonical colored
`3/4`-partition of `V₂`"* (first summand of `Babai.DesignOutcomes`) or *"a UPCC canonically
embedded on a subset `W ⊆ V₂` with `|W| ≥ (3/4)n₂`"* (second summand).  The statement is
made for an arbitrary normalized form `N'` of the Design Lemma, which is what step 1
produces.

The cost `n₂²` is one call of Procedure Reduce-Part2-by-Color (cost `n₂`, Case 3a2 and,
through Cor. 3.4.10 of the original's fill, Case 3a1) and one call of §9.8 (cost `n₂`,
*"If it selects `W`, go to Sec. 9.8"*).

**Proved.**  The proof is one call of the common exit of §9.7,
`Babai.findsAtMultCost_restrictHint` (`Workspace/SplitOrJohnson/BlkExit.lean`), at the
selected part `Babai.designSel` and the hint `Babai.designHint`
(`Workspace/SplitOrJohnson/Step97Select.lean`).  The mathematics of the two sub-cases is
`Babai.case_9_7_3a1` and `Babai.case_9_7_3a2` (`Workspace/SplitOrJohnson/BlockDesign.lean`).

*What the exit is applied to* (`Workspace/SplitOrJohnson/BlkRestrict.lean`).  The exit
*"significant progress: `n₂` is reduced"* is built once, for all three branches of §9.7
that take it:

* `Babai.BlkCaseObj.blkFam` reads a set of blocks back off the ambient type `Set Ω` — the
 carrier of the UPCC of Case 3a2, or a color class of the colored `3/4`-partition of
 Case 3a1, is a subset of `Babai.BlkCaseObj.blkAmb` — as a sub-family of
 `Babai.BlkCaseObj.blocks`, with `Babai.BlkCaseObj.ncard_blkFam` and
 `Babai.BlkCaseObj.blkFam_union_cover` for the pair `(W, V₂ ∖ W)`;
* `Babai.BlkCaseObj.linkGraph` is the bipartite graph `X = (V₁, V₂; Rᵢ)` of §9.7 as an
 object of `Babai.VColBipBlk`, with `Babai.BlkCaseObj.linkGraph_noTwins` (*"no twins in
 `V₁`"*, through `Babai.BlkCaseObj.nbhd_injective`);
* `Babai.reducePart2ByColorBlk` and `Babai.reducePart2ByColorBlk_spec` are Procedure
 Reduce-Part2-by-Color and Lemma 9.3.2 for that graph;
* `Babai.restrictObj`, `Babai.restrictObj_pred` and `Babai.good97_restrict` turn the
 selected part `U` into an object of `Babai.BipBlockInputs` and, when `10|U| ≤ 9n₂`, into
 an outcome `Babai.Good97`.

*The exits that re-enter §9.6 or §9.8 now have an outcome.*  Of the four sub-branches of
Case 3a, the two that reduce `n₂` on the spot are closed by `Babai.good97_restrict` (or by
`Babai.good97_restrict_hint_small`): Case 3a2 with `V₂ ∖ W` selected, where `|U| ≤ n₂/4`,
and Case 3a1 with a selected class of at most `3n₂/4` blocks.  The other two —
*"apply Procedure ImprimitiveCase"* (Case 3a1, selected class larger than `3n₂/4`) and
*"go to Sec. 9.8"* (Case 3a2, `W` selected) — **return the restricted instance with the
hint set**, which is the third kind of major progress of §9.5, *"`X₂` moves from clique to
UPCC while `n₂` does not increase"*.  Entries 88 and 94 of the corrected paper the
repair; what it needs is now built:

* `Babai.VColBipBlk.restrictBlkHint`, `Babai.restrictObjHint`,
 `Babai.restrictObjHint_pred`, `Babai.restrictOutcomeHint`, `Babai.good97_restrict_hint`
 and `Babai.good97_restrict_hint_small`
 (`Workspace/SplitOrJohnson/BlkRestrictHint.lean`): the restriction to a sub-family `U`
 of the blocks with a given coloring `c` of the ordered pairs of blocks of `U` attached
 as the hint.  It is an admissible input of Theorem 9.2.2 under exactly the hypotheses of
 `Babai.restrictObj_pred`, because the symmetry defect of `V₁` does not see the hint
 (`Babai.VColBipBlk.symDefect₁_congr`); it is canonical when `c` is
 (`Babai.VColBipBlk.restrictBlkHint_isIsoTo`); and it has `|U|` blocks.
* The two constructors of the hint (`Workspace/SplitOrJohnson/HintBuild.lean`).  Case 3a2:
 a UPCC is homogeneous of rank `≥ 3`
 (`Babai.PartitionStructure.isHomogeneous_and_rank_of_isUniprimitive`).  Cases 3a1 and
 3b: `Babai.eqvConfig`, the rank-`3` homogeneous coherent configuration of a partition
 into classes of one common size `≥ 2`, with at least two classes
 (`Babai.eqvConfig_isCoherent`, `Babai.eqvConfig_isHomogeneous`).  Either of them is a
 hint through `Babai.hintColoring` and
 `Babai.VColBipBlk.hasHint_restrictBlkHint`.  The hint is not vacuous:
 `Babai.HintExample.X_hasHint` is an object with four blocks in two pairs.
* `Babai.colorSplit` (`Workspace/SplitOrJohnson/ColorSplit.lean`): **which two parts
 Procedure Reduce-Part2-by-Color is applied to in Case 3a1**, where what the Design Lemma
 hands over is a coloring of `V₂` with any number of classes and the procedure takes only
 two parts.  The first part is the class of the least color whose class is at least a
 quarter of the blocks, if there is one, and otherwise the union of the classes of the
 colors up to the least `k` that makes that union a quarter.  Then the second part is at
 most `3n₂/4` (`Babai.four_mul_ncard_compl_colorSplit_le`) and the first part is at most
 `3n₂/4` or is a single color class (`Babai.colorSplit_alternative`) — which is exactly
 what the original's sentence *"if color class selected is greater than `3n₂/4`, this
 color class is equipartitioned"* presupposes.  The choice is canonical
 (`Babai.colorSplit_image`), because it names the part by color values only.

*The bookkeeping that glues these together* is
`Workspace/SplitOrJohnson/Step97Design.lean` and
`Workspace/SplitOrJohnson/Step97Select.lean`:

1. (`Workspace/SplitOrJohnson/Step97Design.lean`): reading the Design Lemma's
  answer off a version is `Babai.designAnswer`, with
  `Babai.designAnswer_isDesignOutcome`; a morphism of
  `(NormalRed.comap S.func N').D` becomes a morphism of `N'.D`
  (`Babai.comapVerHom`) whose underlying map is `Babai.BlkCaseObj.blkAmbEquiv`, and
  `hG'.map_restrict` then gives `Babai.mem_designAnswer_image`;
2. for the carrier: `Babai.blkFam_designAnswer_image` and
  `Babai.blkFam_compl_designAnswer_image` are the hypothesis `hU` of
  `Babai.VColBipBlk.restrictBlk_isIsoTo` and
  `Babai.VColBipBlk.restrictBlkHint_isIsoTo` for the two parts `(W, V₂ ∖ W)`; the same
  for the *coloring* carried on the answer — the UPCC coloring of Case 3a2 and the
  colored partition of Case 3a1 — is `Babai.designHint_image`, and for the part handed
  to Procedure Reduce-Part2-by-Color `Babai.designFirst_image` and
  `Babai.designSel_image`;
3. in Case 3a1, the refinement of Prop. 7.1.3
  (`Babai.ColoredPartition.equipartRefine`), which makes the returned colored
  `3/4`-partition an **equipartition** with the same blocks
  (`Babai.ColoredPartition.block_equipartRefine`), so that the blocks inside the selected
  class have one common size — the hypothesis `hm` of `Babai.eqvConfig`; that the size is
  `≥ 2` is admissibility (Def. 7.1.1) and that there are at least two classes is
  `ρ(Π) ≤ (3/4)n₂ < |C|`.  This is `Babai.hasHint_designSel_eqv`, and Case 3a2's hint is
  `Babai.hasHint_designSel_upcc`.  The choice between the two kinds of progress is
  `Babai.designSel_prog`.

The cost `n₂²` stays; it is an upper bound.  It was meant to pay for the calls of §9.6 and
§9.8 made inside this step, and those calls now happen in the **next** turn of the
recursion, which the hint bit of `Babai.measure_9_5` pays for (entry 94 of
the corrected paper).

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Proposition 2.4.11 (PDF p. 22) — §9.7, **Cases 3a1 and 3a2**, the two sub-cases of Case 3a.  (Version 2.5, lines 4281–4294.)

decls.name: branch_9_4_9_design
decls.docstring:
§9.4, step 9(ii).  **The branch of §9.7** (the block design case).

The branch splits once more, on whether the **input of the pass** carries the hint
(`Babai.HasHintAt`), which is an isomorphism invariant (`Babai.hasHintAt_congr`), so the
split is into full subcategories.

* The input carries the hint: §9.7 is not called.  The blocks that step 8 leaves form a
 clique of the hint, so there are at most `n₂/2` of them — the argument of Case 3a2 of
 §9.7 — and the recursion runs on the instance step 8 leaves
 (`Babai.branch_9_4_9_design_hint`).
* The input has no hint: §9.7 is called through `Babai.step9DesignFunc`, at a cost below
 one turn (`Babai.caseCost_9_7_le_turnCost`).  Its outcome `Babai.IsBlkDesignOutcome` is a
 solution for `(α_new, W₁)`, which transfers to `(α, V₁)`, or a smaller instance that
 already carries `α_new' |V₁'| = α_new |W₁|` and either `10 n₂' ≤ 9 n₂` or the hint; the
 recursion `hrec` applies to it and `Babai.caseCost_mul_costRec_9_7_le` pays for the call,
 using the bit `1` of the input (`Babai.branch_9_4_9_design_nohint`).

Why the first branch does not call §9.7: a pass that starts from a hinted instance and only
gains the hint again would not make the progress that §9.5 asks for.  See entries 88 and 94
of the corrected paper.

decls.name: bruteForceThreshold
decls.docstring:
§11.3, steps 1–2: **the absolute constant `C₀` of the brute-force exit**, read as a
bound on the window.

Step 2 of Procedure Reduce-to-Johnson exits when `|G| < C₀` for an absolute constant `C₀`.
A window of fewer than

> `N₀ = max{64, n₀!}`

points has `|G^Δ| ≤ N₀!`, which is such a constant, so the test of step 2 succeeds there.
The two parts of the maximum are the two places where a constant is needed: `64` is the
threshold of `Babai.JohnsonCaseData.window_large`, and `n₀!` bounds `|Ḡ|` on a block system
with fewer than `n₀` blocks, which is where Theorem 11.2.1 does not apply
(`Babai.descentThreshold`).

`N₀` is fixed **before** the instance, the group and the strings, which is what
*"absolute constant"* means.

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Theorem 11.2.1 (PDF p. 93) — §11.3, steps 1–2: **the absolute constant `C₀` of the brute-force exit**, read as a bound on the window.

decls.name: cameronStructure_polyTime
decls.docstring:
§11.2, the algorithmic part of Theorem 11.2.1, cited from [BaLS].

Quoted from the paper (version 2.5, lines 5027–5029):

> The algorithmic part is well known: Cameron groups can be recognized and their structure
> mapped out in polynomial time (and even in NC [BaLS]).

There is a polynomial-time routine that takes generators of `G ≤ S_n`.  Whenever `G` is a
Cameron group, it returns parameters `s`, `t`, `k` and a bijection of the domain with
`(Fin k choose t)^s` such that `G` is a Cameron group with these parameters through this
bijection (Def. 11.2.2).  The module docstring says how each phrase of the paper is read.

links.rationale: Formalizes Theorem 11.2.1 (PDF p. 93) — §11.2, the algorithmic part of Theorem 11.2.1, cited from [BaLS].

decls.docstring:

distinct vertices is at most `n^k`, where `n = |Ω|`.

The count is `∑_{ℓ < k} n(n−1)…(n−ℓ+1)`, one summand per length; each summand is at most
`n^ℓ`, and `∑_{ℓ < k} n^ℓ ≤ n^k` for `n ≥ 2` (`sum_pow_lt_succ_le`).  The hypothesis
`n ≥ 2` cannot be dropped: for `n = 1` and `k ≥ 2` there are two admissible strings and
`n^k = 1`.  Theorem 8.1.2 assumes `2 ≤ k ≤ n/2`.

decls.name: case_9_6_1_step2
decls.docstring:
Lemma 9.6.1, step 2 of Procedure ImprimitiveCase.  *"We shall see that one of these is
always possible without reducing the symmetry defect on `V₁` below `1/2`."*

Either some `Zᵢ` has symmetry defect at least `1/2` on `V₁`, which is branch 2(i)
(*"`Y ← Zᵢ`"*), or the contracted graph of branch 2(ii) has symmetry defect at least `1/2`
on `V₁`.

Paper's proof: if branch 2(i) does not apply then the symmetry defect of `V₁` in every
`Zᵢ` is less than `1/2`, so *"for each `i ≤ m` there is a (unique) `Zᵢ`-twin equivalence
class `Cᵢ ⊆ V₁` such that `|Cᵢ| > n₁/2`"*
(`BipGraph.lt_two_mul_symmetricity₁_of_defect_lt_half` together with
`BipGraph.exists_twinSet_card_eq_symmetricity₁`); the vertices of `Cᵢ` are twins in `Zᵢ`,
so they have the same `R_j`-neighborhood in `Bᵢ`
(`BipGraph.twinSet₁_nbhd_iff`); and then Lemma 9.6.2 applies.

Uniqueness of `Cᵢ` is not needed and is not stated: any set of twins with more than `n₁/2`
elements does the work, and by `BipGraph.exists_twinSet_card_eq_symmetricity₁` a largest
one is such a set.

As in `lemma_9_6_2`, the semiregularity of the contraction (Cor. 3.4.9) and the
non-emptiness of `R_h` are hypotheses, exactly as the paper takes them from §3.4.

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Theorem 3.4.9 (Contraction) (PDF p. 37) — Lemma 9.6.1, step 2 of Procedure ImprimitiveCase.  *"We shall see that one of these is always possible without reducing the symmetry defect on `V₁` below `1/2`."*

decls.name: case_9_7
decls.docstring:
§9.7 (block design case).  *"Assumptions: no twins in `V₁`, `X₂` is the clique
configuration (rank-2)."*  (Version 2.5, lines 4234-4290.)

At the multiplicative cost of the Design Lemma — *"Apply the Design lemma to `H`, viewed as
a `d₁`-ary relational structure.  (Multiplicative cost `n₂^{d₁} < n₂^{(7/3) log₂ n₁}`.)"*,
Case 3a — the block design case either finishes Theorem 9.2.2 on `V₁` or makes major
progress in the sense of §9.5.

The threshold `α` and the number `n₂` in the outcome are those **of the input**
(`Babai.BlkBlockDesignInputs.alpha`, `Babai.BlkBlockDesignInputs.numBlocks`).  An earlier
form of this statement had `α` and a bound `N` on the measure as parameters of the theorem;
that form could not be applied at step 9 of §9.4, where `α` is `Babai.alphaNew` of the
input, and for `N = 0` it asked for more than §9.7 gives.

The exponent is `7 (⌊log₂ n₁⌋ + 1)/3 + 2`.  The paper's `d₁ ≤ (7/3) log₂ n₁` is with the
real logarithm, and `log₂ n₁ ≤ ⌊log₂ n₁⌋ + 1`.  The two extra factors `n₂` are the
multiplicative cost of Procedure Reduce-Part2-by-Color (at most `n₂`) and of §9.8
(*"The multiplicative cost is `n₂`"*), which Case 3a2 calls.

The proof is the case distinction of §9.7 — Case 1, Case 2, Case 3a, Case 3b — glued by
`Babai.FindsAtMultCost.cases`, whose hypothesis that the branch condition is an isomorphism
invariant is `Babai.BlkBlockDesignInputs.case1P_congr`,
`Babai.BlkBlockDesignInputs.case2P_congr` and
`Babai.BlkBlockDesignInputs.case3aP_congr` (all proved).  The four branches are
`Babai.case_9_7_case1`, `Babai.case_9_7_case2`, `Babai.case_9_7_case3a'` and
`Babai.case_9_7_case3b'`; all four are proved.

decls.name: case_9_7_1
decls.docstring:
Case 1 of §9.7.  *"`V₂` is a set of twins in `H`.  This means `Aut(H)` acts on `V₂` as
`S(V₂)`.  Since `H` has no multiple edges and is uniform of rank `d₁`, it follows that `H`
is the complete `d₁`-uniform hypergraph.  Let us label `v ∈ V₁` by the set `X(v)`.  This
establishes a bijection between `V₁` and the set `(V₂ choose d₁)`.  Since isomorphisms
preserve the number of common neighbors, this correspondence gives a canonical embedding of
the Johnson scheme `J(n₂, d₁)` on `V₁`, achieving goal (b) of Theorem 9.2.2."*
(Version 2.5, lines 4240–4251.)

Goal (b) asks for a **nontrivial** Johnson scheme, i.e. an object of `JohnsonSchemes`
(Defs. 3.2.9/3.2.13, with `2 ≤ t` and `2t + 1 ≤ k`), so the conclusion is stated in the
shape of `IsJohnsonColoring`: a bijection `φ : V₁ ≃ (V₂ choose d₁)` under which the edge
coloring `d₁ - |X(u) ∩ X(v)|` of `V₁` (the paper's *"isomorphisms preserve the number of
common neighbors"*) is the Johnson coloring `|φ(u) \ φ(v)|` of `J(n₂, d₁)`, together with
`2 ≤ d₁` and `2d₁ + 1 ≤ n₂`.

§9.7 checks neither of the last two, and both are needed for goal (b); see the entry
"§9.7 Case 1" in the corrected paper.  `2 ≤ d₁` follows from the standing hypothesis
`|V₂| < α|V₁|` of Theorem 9.2.2 (`case_9_7_1_two_le_d₁`).  `2d₁ + 1 ≤ n₂` comes from
outside Case 1 — from the primitivity of `X₁`, established in step 6 of Procedure Bipartite
Split-or-Johnson: for `n₂ = 2d₁` the Johnson coloring of `J(2d₁, d₁)` has the disconnected
constituent `|S \ T| = d₁` (a perfect matching), and `X₁`, which refines that coloring,
would then have a disconnected non-diagonal constituent — so it is carried as a hypothesis
here, and both are repeated in the conclusion, where goal (b) needs them.

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Theorem 9.2.2 (Bipartite Split-or-Johnson) (PDF p. 72) — Case 1 of §9.7.  *"`V₂` is a set of twins in `H`.  This means `Aut(H)` acts on `V₂` as `S(V₂)`.  Since `H` has no multiple edges and is uniform of rank `d₁`, it follows that `H` is the complete `d₁`-uniform hypergraph...

decls.name: case_9_7_1_two_le_d₁
decls.docstring:
Case 1 of §9.7, a step the paper does not check: `d₁ ≥ 2`, which goal (b) needs
(Def. 3.2.9 excludes `t = 1`, and by Remark 3.2.15 the Johnson schemes `J(k,1)` are the
clique configurations, i.e. trivial).

In Case 1 the map `v ↦ X(v)` is a bijection of `V₁` onto the `d₁`-subsets of `V₂`, so
`n₁ = C(n₂, d₁)`.  The standing hypothesis of Theorem 9.2.2 is `n₂ < αn₁` with `α < 1`,
hence `n₂ < n₁`.  But `d₁ = 0` gives `n₁ = 1 ≤ n₂`, and `d₁ = 1` gives `n₁ = n₂` (the
paper's *"perfect matching"*); both contradict `n₂ < n₁`.

decls.name: case_9_7_2
decls.docstring:
Case 2 of §9.7.  *"There is an `H`-twin equivalence class `C ⊆ V₂` of size
`|C| ≥ n₂/2`.  So `S(C) ≤ Aut(H)`. … Apply procedure Reduce-Part2-by-Color to the coloring
`(C, V₂ \ C)`.  If `V₂ \ C` is selected, we have made significant progress (reduced `|V₂|`
by half).  If `C` is selected, let `X' = X[V₁, C]` … Color each vertex of `V₁` by the size
of the corresponding hyperedge in `H'` … If all `c'`-color classes have size less than
`αn₁`, return this coloring, exit.  Otherwise, let `A ⊆ V₁` be the dominant `c'`-color
class, so `|A| ≥ αn₁ > n₁/2` … `X*` is semiregular.  It cannot be trivial because the
relative sizes of `A` (in `V₁`) and `C` (in `V₂`) add up to more than 1, contradicting
Cor. 2.4.32. … Since `Aut(H*)` acts on `C` as the symmetric group, all edges of `H*` have
the same multiplicity.  In other words, `A` is equipartitioned by the twin equivalence
classes in `X*`.  If this is a nontrivial partition, return this partition, exit. … the
only remaining option is that there are no twins in `A`, i.e. `E*` has no multiple edges.
Since `C` is a set of twins in `H*`, we are back to Case 1."*
(Version 2.5, lines 4252–4274.)

The step of Case 2 that is not bookkeeping is the non-triviality of `X*`, and the paper's
reason for it is the hypothesis stated here: *"the relative sizes of `A` (in `V₁`) and `C`
(in `V₂`) add up to more than 1"*.  At the call site `|A| ≥ αn₁ > n₁/2` and `|C| ≥ n₂/2`;
the second of these is not strict, so the hypothesis has to be the sum of the two relative
sizes, not the two halves separately.

decls.name: case_9_7_3a1
decls.docstring:
Case 3a1 of §9.7, with the missing reference `Cor. ??` filled from the original
version (`babai-gi.tex`, lines 3981–3992).

Version 2.5 (lines 4281–4284): *"The Design lemma returns a canonical colored
`3/4`-partition of `V₂`.  Apply Cor. ??.  Significant progress is made in time, polynomial
in `n₁`, namely, `n₂` is reduced to `≤ 3n₂/4`.  If a multiplicative cost of `m` is
incurred, the progress is more significant: `n₂` is reduced to `≤ n₂/m` (`2 ≤ m ≤ n₂/2`)."*

Original: *"Recompute `X` and thereby `X₂`.  Colored `(3/4)`-partition on `V₂` persists
(colors can only get refined).  Apply Reduce-Part2-by-Color to the coloring.  If color
class selected is greater than `3n₂/4`, this color class is equipartitioned; apply
Procedure ImprimitiveCase (Sec. 9.6).  In either case, significant progress: `n₂` reduced
to `≤ 3n₂/4`."*

Here `C₁`, `C₂` are the two unions of color classes to which Reduce-Part2-by-Color is
applied, and `hsmall` is the property of a colored `3/4`-partition `Π` of `V₂` that the
paper uses: each of the two parts either has size `≤ (3/4)n₂` already, or is one color
class of `Π`, and then the blocks of `Π` inside it are a partition into at least two
blocks, each of size `≥ 2` (admissibility, Def. 7.1.1) and `≤ (3/4)n₂` (`ρ(Π) ≤ (3/4)n₂`),
which is exactly the input of Procedure ImprimitiveCase (§9.6).  The conclusion is that the
*selected* part `U` keeps the symmetry defect of `V₁` at `≥ (n₁ - 1)/2` (Lemma 9.3.2) and
has that same property, which is the *"significant progress: `n₂` reduced to `≤ 3n₂/4`"*.

The three conditions on the blocks are what makes the second alternative say something:
without `2 ≤ |Q|` and `1 < |P|` it is satisfied by the partition of `D` into singletons,
for any `D`, and the alternative would be vacuous.  Both come from the colored
`3/4`-partition: `2 ≤ |Q|` is `ColoredPartition.IsAdmissible` for a color class of size
`≥ 2`, and `1 < |P|` holds because a single block would have size `|D| > (3/4)n₂ ≥ ρ(Π)`.

decls.name: case_9_7_3a2
decls.docstring:
Case 3a2 of §9.7.  *"The Design lemma returns a UPCC `Y` canonically embedded on a
subset `W ⊆ V₂` with `|W| ≥ (3/4)n₂`.  Apply Reduce-Part2-by-Color to the partition
`(W, V₂ \ W)`.  If the procedure selects `V₂ \ W`, significant progress (`n₂` reduced to
`≤ n₂/4`).  If it selects `W`, go to Sec. 9.8.  Let `U ⊆ V₂` be the part selected, and
`(X₂)_new` the homogeneous coherent configuration obtained on `U`.  If `(X₂)_new` is a
UPCC, exit, significant progress.  If `(X₂)_new` is not a UPCC, i.e. it has rank 2, then
`U` was a clique in `Y` and therefore `|U| ≤ |W|/2 ≤ n₂/2` by Prop. 2.4.11, a significant
reduction of `|V₂|`."*  (Version 2.5, lines 4285–4294.)

The step with mathematical content is the last one, and it is Prop. 2.4.11: a rank-2
`(X₂)_new` means that `U` carries no edge of the non-diagonal constituent of `Y` that it
would otherwise carry, i.e. `U` is an independent set of that constituent, which is a
non-empty biregular digraph on `W`; hence `2|U| ≤ |W|`.

decls.name: case_9_7_3a_cost
decls.docstring:
Case 3a of §9.7.  *"`d₁ ≤ (7/3) log₂ n₁`.  Apply the Design lemma to `H`, viewed as a
`d₁`-ary relational structure.  (Multiplicative cost `n₂^{d₁} < n₂^{(7/3)log₂ n₁}`.)"*
(Version 2.5, lines 4276–4280.)

The content of the parenthesis is the monotonicity of the exponent, which is what makes the
cost of the Design Lemma call quasipolynomial in `n₁`.  The cost itself is a running-time
claim; see the entry of kind "pending" in the corrected paper.

decls.name: case_9_7_3b_t_le
decls.docstring:
Case 3b of §9.7.  *"`d₁ > 7/3 log₂ n₁`.  Let `t = ⌈(7/4) log₂ n₁⌉`.  So
`t ≤ (3/4)d₁`."*  (Version 2.5, lines 4295–4301.)

**The paper's `t` does not satisfy `t ≤ (3/4)d₁`.**  Writing `L = log₂ n₁`, Case 3b only
gives `d₁ > (7/3)L`, so `(3/4)d₁ > (7/4)L`, and rounding `(7/4)L` *up* can overshoot that
margin.  Counterexample: `n₁ = 11`, `L = 3.4594…`, `(7/3)L = 8.072…`, so `d₁ = 9` is a
legal Case 3b value (and `d₁ ≤ n₂ < n₁` allows it, e.g. `n₂ = 10`); then
`t = ⌈(7/4)L⌉ = ⌈6.054…⌉ = 7`, while `(3/4)d₁ = 6.75 < 7`.  The same happens for a positive
fraction of all `n₁`.  See the entry "§9.7 Case 3b, `t ≤ (3/4)d₁`" in the corrected paper.

Rounding `(7/4)L` up is exactly what breaks the printed inequality, so `t` is kept as the
paper defines it and the **upper bound is relaxed to the ceiling**: from `(7/3)L < d₁` one
gets `(7/4)L < (3/4)d₁`, hence `t = ⌈(7/4)L⌉ ≤ ⌈(3/4)d₁⌉` by monotonicity of the ceiling.
That is enough for Lemma 2.5.12, which is proved here in the form
`Babai.Hypergraph.skeleton_defect` with the hypothesis `t ≤ ⌈(3/4)d⌉`: its proof uses the
upper bound only to pick a `t`-subset of `S ∩ E` with `|S ∩ E| ≥ (3/4)d`, and `|S ∩ E|` is
an integer, so `|S ∩ E| ≥ ⌈(3/4)d⌉ ≥ t`.

The second conclusion, `t < (7/4)L + 1`, is the upper bound on `t` that keeps the
multiplicative cost `n₂^t` of the Design Lemma call quasipolynomial in `n₁`.

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Lemma 2.5.12 (Skeleton defect lemma) (PDF p. 28) — Case 3b of §9.7.  *"`d₁ > 7/3 log₂ n₁`.  Let `t = ⌈(7/4) log₂ n₁⌉`.  So `t ≤ (3/4)d₁`."*  (Version 2.5, lines 4295–4301.)

decls.name: case_9_7_case1
decls.docstring:
Case 1 of §9.7.  *"`V₂` is a set of twins in `H`. … Let us label `v ∈ V₁` by the set
`X(v)`.  This establishes a bijection between `V₁` and the set `(V₂ choose d₁)`. … this
correspondence gives a canonical embedding of the Johnson scheme `J(n₂, d₁)` on `V₁`,
achieving goal (b) of Theorem 9.2.2.  With this we not only exit this routine but exit the
main algorithm."*  (Version 2.5, lines 4240–4251.)

No choice is made, so the cost is `1`; it is weakened to the common cost of
`Babai.case_9_7` here.

**Proved.**  The construction is `Babai.case1Outcome`: the single outcome is the Johnson
scheme on `V₁` itself, so the reduction is `Babai.FindsAtMultCost.of_outcomes_sub` with a
one-member tuple, and the cost `1` is below the common cost of `Babai.case_9_7` because
`n₂ ≥ 1`.  Its four ingredients are

* *"`H` is the complete `d₁`-uniform hypergraph"*: `Babai.isCase1_mem_edgeFam`, by
 induction on `|S ∖ T|` — one transposition of blocks replaces a member of `S ∖ T` by a
 member of `T ∖ S`, and `Babai.BlkCaseObj.IsCase1` says that every such transposition
 preserves `Babai.BlkCaseObj.edgeFam`.
* *"This establishes a bijection between `V₁` and `(V₂ choose d₁)`"*:
 `Babai.BlkCaseObj.labelEquiv`, whose injectivity is
 `Babai.BlkCaseObj.nbhd_injective` (*"no multiple edges because there are no twins in
 `V₁`"*) and whose well-definedness is `Babai.BlkCaseObj.nbhd_ncard_uniform`
 (*"uniform of rank `d₁`"*).
* The parameters.  `Babai.two_le_and_add_two_le_of_lt_choose`, applied to
 `n₁ = C(n₂, d₁)` and `n₂ < n₁`, gives `2 ≤ d₁` **and** `d₁ + 2 ≤ n₂` — the first is the
 paper's missing check (entry 41 of the corrected paper), the second is what the complementary
 labels need; the boundary `n₂ = 2d₁` is `Babai.BlkCaseObj.numBlocks_ne_two_mul_d₁`.
* The labels.  `Babai.isJohnsonColoring_of_labels` builds the object of
 `Babai.JohnsonSchemes` under either of the two alternatives of
 `Babai.johnson_alternative`: `2d₁ + 1 ≤ n₂`, which is the paper's `J(n₂, d₁)`, or
 `2(n₂ − d₁) + 1 ≤ n₂`, where the labels are replaced by their complements `V₂ ∖ X(v)`
 and the scheme is `J(n₂, n₂ − d₁)` (entry 82 of the corrected paper).

Three of these ingredients rest on the named lemmas
`Babai.BlkCaseObj.nbhd_ncard_uniform`, `Babai.BlkCaseObj.nbhd_injective` and
`Babai.BlkCaseObj.numBlocks_ne_two_mul_d₁`, which read the situation of §9.7 off the
coherent configuration of step 3 of §9.4.

This establishes a bijection between `V₁` and the set `(V₂ choose d₁)`. … this correspondence gives a canonical embedding o...

decls.name: case_9_7_case2
decls.docstring:
Case 2 of §9.7.  *"There is an `H`-twin equivalence class `C ⊆ V₂` of size
`|C| ≥ n₂/2`.  So `S(C) ≤ Aut(H)`. … Apply procedure Reduce-Part2-by-Color to the coloring
`(C, V₂ \ C)`.  If `V₂ \ C` is selected, we have made significant progress (reduced `|V₂|`
by half).  If `C` is selected, … If all `c'`-color classes have size less than `αn₁`,
return this coloring, exit.  Otherwise, let `A ⊆ V₁` be the dominant `c'`-color class … If
this is a nontrivial partition, return this partition, exit. … we are back to Case 1.
Proceed as in Case 1, exit."*  (Version 2.5, lines 4252–4274.)

The cost is the one call of Procedure Reduce-Part2-by-Color, `n₂`; it is weakened to the
common cost of `Babai.case_9_7` here.

**`C` is made canonical first.**  The branch condition
`Babai.BlkCaseObj.IsCase2` is the paper's, an existential, while every object this branch
returns is built from `C` and must therefore be carried along by every morphism.  The twin
classes of `Aut(H)` partition `V₂` canonically (`Babai.BlkCaseObj.isHTwin_refl`,
`.isHTwin_symm`, `.isHTwin_trans`), so `C` is determined unless two classes tie.
`Babai.BlkCaseObj.bigTwin`, the union of the classes of size `≥ n₂/2`, is the class when it
is unique (`Babai.BlkCaseObj.bigTwin_spec`) and is all of `V₂` in the tie
(`Babai.BlkCaseObj.tie_spec'`); the test `bigTwin = V₂` separates the two and is an
isomorphism invariant (`Babai.case2TieP_congr`).  See the entry on §9.7 Case 2 in
the corrected paper.

**Status.**  All the exits are **proved**: the tie (`Babai.case_9_7_case2_tie`),
*"if `V₂ ∖ C` is selected"* (`Babai.case_9_7_case2_compl`), *"if all `c'`-color classes
have size less than `αn₁`, return this coloring"* (`Babai.case_9_7_case2_small`), and the
exits at the dominant `c'`-color class (`Babai.case_9_7_case2_dom`).

decls.docstring:
§9.7, Case 2.  *"Apply procedure Reduce-Part2-by-Color to the coloring `(C, V₂ ∖ C)`.
If `V₂ ∖ C` is selected, we have made significant progress (reduced `|V₂|` by half)."*
(Version 2.5, lines 4256-4258.)

`|C| ≥ n₂/2`, so `|V₂ ∖ C| ≤ n₂/2` and `10|V₂ ∖ C| ≤ 5n₂ ≤ 9n₂`: the first alternative of

covering `V₂ = C ∪ (V₂ ∖ C)`, whose other alternative is the negated branch condition
(`Babai.BlkCaseObj.symDefect₁_compl_bigTwin`).

decls.name: case_9_7_case2_dom
decls.docstring:
§9.7, Case 2, the two exits at the **dominant `c'`-color class** `A` (version 2.5,
lines 4264-4274).

**Proved.**  The branch condition is that some `c'`-color class has at least `αn₁` points;
*"let `A ⊆ V₁` be the dominant `c'`-color class, so `|A| ≥ αn₁ > n₁/2"*, which is
`Babai.BlkCaseObj.domClass` (it is canonical because `α > 1/2` leaves at most one such
class).  The paper's route is

* *"Let `X* = X[A, C]` … So `X*` is semiregular.  It cannot be trivial because the relative
 sizes of `A` (in `V₁`) and `C` (in `V₂`) add up to more than 1, contradicting
 Cor. 2.4.32."* — `Babai.case_9_7_2`, applied to the link through

 `Babai.BlkCaseObj.linkBipGraph_not_isTrivial`; the conclusion is `1 ≤ d* < |C|`
 (`Babai.BlkCaseObj.DomHyp.one_le_localSize`, `.localSize_lt`).
* *"Since `Aut(H*)` acts on `C` as the symmetric group, all edges of `H*` have the same
 multiplicity. … If this is a nontrivial partition, return this partition, exit."* —

`Babai.restrictObjHint_pred` is the input's own: `V₁` has no twins in the link
(`Babai.BlkCaseObj.linkGraph_noTwins`), so Lemma 9.3.2 at the trivial covering
`V₂ = V₂ ∪ V₂` gives a symmetry defect of `n₁ − 1 ≥ (n₁ − 1)/2`
(`Babai.BlkCaseObj.symDefect₁_blocks`).

`2 ≤ m` is `Babai.BlkCaseObj.tie_spec'`: `m = 1` would give `n₂ = 2` and hence
`n₁ ≤ C(2, d₁) ≤ 2`, against `n₂ < n₁`.

decls.name: case_9_7_case3a
decls.docstring:
Case 3a of §9.7.  *"`d₁ ≤ (7/3) log₂ n₁`.  Apply the Design lemma to `H`, viewed as a
`d₁`-ary relational structure.  (Multiplicative cost `n₂^{d₁} < n₂^{(7/3)log₂ n₁}`.)"*,
with its two sub-cases 3a1 and 3a2.  (Version 2.5, lines 4276–4294.)

The cost is `n₂^{d₁}` for the Design Lemma call, times `n₂` for Procedure
Reduce-Part2-by-Color and `n₂` for the call of §9.8 in Case 3a2.

**Proved.**  The proof is

* `Babai.FindsAtMultCost.ofFibers` for the invariant `d'`, which is an isomorphism
 invariant (`Babai.BlkCaseObj.IsMorphOn.d'_eq`) and bounded by `|Ω|` because the blocks
 are non-empty and pairwise disjoint (`Babai.BlkCaseObj.n₂_le_card`).  On the fiber
 `{d' = N}` (`Babai.Case3aFiber`) the arity of the Design Lemma is the constant `N`,
 which is what the fixed-arity statement of Theorem 8.1.2 needs;
* on a fiber, `Babai.case_9_7_case3a_fiber`: step 1
 (`Babai.case_9_7_case3a_step1`, the Design Lemma call, cost `n₂^{d'}`) composed with
 step 2 (the two sub-cases, cost `n₂²`) by `Babai.FindsAtMultCost.comp`.

**The transfer of the Design Lemma to the blocks** is
`Workspace/SplitOrJohnson/BlockDesignHyper.lean`.  `Babai.designLemma_finds_designInputs`
is a reduction over the ambient type `Set Ω`, where a block is a **point**
(`Babai.BlkCaseObj.blkAmb`); `Babai.NormalRed.comap` (`Workspace/Functors/Ambient.lean`)
pulls it back along the functor `Babai.BlkDesignSetup.func`, which in Case 3a assigns to an input of §9.7 the
neighborhood hypergraph `H` read as a `d'`-ary relational structure
(`Babai.BlkCaseObj.nbhdStruct`).  The three hypotheses of Theorem 8.1.2 are checked in
`Babai.BlkCaseObj.designObj`:

* *"`2 ≤ k`"* and *"`k ≤ n/2`"* at the rank `d' = min(d₁, n₂ − d₁)`
 (`Babai.BlkCaseObj.two_le_d'`, `Babai.BlkCaseObj.two_mul_d'_le_n₂`).  §9.7 checks
 neither, and `d₁` itself need not satisfy the second; `H` is therefore complemented when
 `d₁ > n₂/2`, which changes neither the automorphism group nor the twins nor the defect
 (`Babai.Hypergraph.compl`, `Babai.Hypergraph.aut_compl`).  See the entry *"§9.7 Case 3:
 the Design Lemma is applied at rank `d₁` without checking `d₁ ≤ n₂/2`"* in
 the corrected paper;
* *"symmetry defect `≥ 1 − α`"*, here `≥ 1/4`, is Case 3 itself, *"the relative symmetry
 defect of `H` is `≥ 1/2`"*: `Babai.BlkCaseObj.IsHTwin` is the twin relation of `Aut(H)`
 (`Babai.BlkCaseObj.twinOrEq_iff_isHTwin`), so the negation of Case 2 bounds every twin
 equivalence class of `Aut(H)` by `n₂/2`, and `Babai.defect_ge_of_twinClass_ncard_le`
 (Obs. 2.3.12) turns that into the defect bound
 (`Babai.BlkCaseObj.defect_nbhdHg_ge`).

`Babai.BlkDesignSetup.func` is a `Babai.Func.IsBlockFunc`
(`Babai.BlkDesignSetup.func_isBlockFunc`): a
morphism acts on the assigned object by `B ↦ f(B)`, which is what makes the way back of
`Babai.FindsAtMultCost.of_comap` available to step 2.

*Note on the transfer, for whoever wrote the first version of this note.*  The obvious
route — apply
`Babai.designLemma_finds` with the ambient type `Set Ω`, so that `H` is an honest `d₁`-ary
structure on `blocks ⊆ Set Ω`, and transfer the resulting `Babai.FindsAtMultCost` back
along the assignment "block `B` ↦ `φ '' B`" — does **not** go through as a change of
ambient type alone.  `Babai.FindsAtMultCost C H cost Good` quantifies over a category
`D : Cat.{0,0} Ω` of tuples **over the same ambient type `Ω` as `C`**, and the objects of
the tuple category produced over `Set Ω` live on subsets of `Set Ω`; they cannot be read as
objects over `Ω`.  So a transfer lemma has to rebuild the reduction rather than reuse it:
the workable shape is a `Babai.NormalRed` of the source category whose extra datum at `X`
is a member of the tuple of the `Set Ω`-reduction at the assigned object (this is a type
over `X.car`, so it is legal).  This is what `Babai.NormalRed.comap` does, and step 1 uses
it with the category of versions itself as the intermediate outcome category, so that the
input is still available to step 2.

decls.name: case_9_7_case3b
decls.docstring:
Case 3b of §9.7.  *"`d₁ > 7/3 log₂ n₁`.  Let `t = ⌈(7/4) log₂ n₁⌉`.  So `t ≤ (3/4)d₁`.
By Lemma 2.5.12, the symmetry defect of the `t`-skeleton `H^{(t)}` of `H` is greater than
`1/4`.  Let us apply the Design lemma to `H^{(t)}`.  If the result is a `3/4`-partition of
`V₂`, ********* an application of Reduce-Part2-by-Color and if necessary, an application of
the imprimitive case.  Else (the result is a UPCC on a subset of `V₂` of size `≥ (3/4)n₂`
(significant progress, exit)."*  (Version 2.5, lines 4295–4301.)

The `*****` is filled from version 2.5's own words (entry 37 of the corrected paper); the
original exits on the partition instead, and version 2.5 governs.  The printed
`t ≤ (3/4)d₁` is false for a positive fraction of the `n₁` and is relaxed to
`t ≤ ⌈(3/4)d₁⌉` (entry 42 of the corrected paper, `Babai.case_9_7_3b_t_le`), which is what
`Babai.Hypergraph.skeleton_defect` (Lemma 2.5.12) needs.

The branch condition is the negation of `Babai.BlkCaseObj.IsCase3a`, which is now read on
`d' = min(d₁, n₂ − d₁)` rather than on `d₁` (see the docstring of
`Babai.BlkCaseObj.d'`).  So here `d' > (7/3) log₂ n₁`, the `t`-skeleton is taken of the
`d'`-uniform hypergraph (`H` or its bipartite complement), and `2t ≤ (3/2)d' ≤ n₂` by
`Babai.BlkCaseObj.two_mul_d'_le_n₂`, which is the hypothesis `k ≤ n/2` of
Theorem 8.1.2.

The cost is `n₂^t` for the Design Lemma call on the `t`-skeleton, times `n₂` for
Reduce-Part2-by-Color and `n₂` for Procedure ImprimitiveCase (§9.6, `Babai.lemma_9_6_1`).

**Proved.**  Case 3b is Case 3a with one hypergraph exchanged for another, so it runs on
the **same** machinery: `Babai.BlkDesignSetup` is the data of a Design Lemma call on the
blocks — the category of inputs, the object of §9.7 under an input, and the `N`-ary
relational structure on the blocks that the Design Lemma is applied to — and
`Babai.blkDesign_fiber` (`Babai.blkDesign_step1` composed with `Babai.blkDesign_step2`)
runs the call and the exit for an arbitrary such setup.  Case 3a instantiates it with `H`
itself at the rank `d'` (`Babai.case3aSetup`), Case 3b with the `t`-skeleton of `H` at the
rank `t` (`Babai.case3bSetup`).  So Case 3b's two exits are Case 3a's, through
`Babai.designSel`, `Babai.designHint` and `Babai.findsAtMultCost_restrictHint`; see the
docstring of `Babai.case_9_7_case3a_step2` for the pieces.

The *input* of the call is built in `Workspace/SplitOrJohnson/BlockDesignSkel.lean`:

* `Babai.BlkCaseObj.tSkel` is `t = ⌈(7/4) log₂ n₁⌉`, with the two bounds the branch needs,
 `Babai.BlkCaseObj.tSkel_le_ceil_d'` (*"`t ≤ (3/4)d₁`"*, at the rank `d'` and with the
 ceiling of entry 42 of the corrected paper) and `Babai.BlkCaseObj.tSkel_lt`;
* `Babai.BlkCaseObj.skeleton_defect_nbhdHg` is Lemma 2.5.12 at the input, *"the symmetry
 defect of the `t`-skeleton `H^{(t)}` of `H` is greater than `1/4`"*.  Lemma 2.5.12 asks
 for a **nontrivial regular** hypergraph, neither of which §9.7 checks:
 `Babai.BlkCaseObj.nbhdHg_not_trivialUniform` reads nontriviality off the negation of
 Case 1 (a trivial uniform hypergraph has `Aut(H) = S(V₂)`, which is Case 1), and
 `Babai.BlkCaseObj.nbhdHg_isRegular` is the semiregularity of the link — the degree of a
 block in `H` is its in-degree in the constituent `Babai.BlkCaseObj.linkColor`, which by
 Obs. 3.3.5 (`Babai.BipCaseData.ncard_inNbhd_eq`) depends only on the vertex color;
* `Babai.BlkCaseObj.skelDesignObj` is the `t`-skeleton as an **admissible input of
 Theorem 8.1.2** at the rank `t` and the threshold `3/4`;
* `Babai.BlkCaseObj.map_skelStruct` makes it a **functor** of the input: the hyperedges of
 the skeleton correspond under `Babai.BlkCaseObj.blkAmbEquiv` because the hyperedges of
 `H` do (`Babai.BlkCaseObj.nbhdHg_edgeSet_image`) and a `t`-set lies inside a hyperedge
 exactly if its image does (`Babai.Hypergraph.mem_skeleton_edgeSet_image`).

The fibering is over `t`, which is an isomorphism invariant because `n₁` is
(`Babai.BlkCaseObj.IsMorphOn.tSkel_eq`) and is bounded by `|Ω|` because `2t ≤ n₂ ≤ |Ω|`
(`Babai.BlkCaseObj.two_mul_tSkel_le_n₂`, `Babai.BlkCaseObj.n₂_le_card`).

decls.name: case_9_8
decls.docstring:
§9.8 (UPCC case).  *"Claim.  Procedure Reduce-by-UPCC makes significant progress.
Specifically, it either achieves goal (a) or reduces `n₂` by half while maintaining
symmetry defect `≥ 1/2` in each part.  The multiplicative cost is `n₂`."*  (Version 2.5,
lines 4318-4322.)

The two outcomes have the same shape as the two outcomes of Lemma 9.6.1 — a canonical
colored `1/2`-partition of `V₁`, or a canonical bipartite graph on `V₁` and at most `n₂/2`
blocks in which the symmetry defect of `V₁` is at least `1/2` — so the outcome predicate is
`Babai.IsBlkImprimitiveOutcome`, the one of §9.6.

The proof is the case distinction of Procedure Reduce-by-UPCC on its branch condition
`Babai.UPCCSplits` (*"if there is no `α`-dominant color in `X₁₂`"*, with `α = 1/2`): the
two branches are `Babai.case_9_8_step1` (step 2 of the procedure, the `x`-local coloring of

decls.name: centralizer_socle_eq_bot
decls.docstring:
Background for Lemma 10.2.5, Case 2: for a primitive group `G` whose socle is
nonabelian, `C_G(Soc(G)) = 1`.  This is what makes the map
`Pker(G) → Aut(R₁) × ⋯ × Aut(R_s)` injective, so that
`Pker(G)/Soc(G) ≤ Out(R₁) × ⋯ × Out(R_s)`.

Proof (elementary): `C_G(N) ⊴ G`, so if it were nontrivial it would contain a minimal
normal subgroup `M` of `G`; then `M ≤ Soc(G) = N`, whence `M ≤ C_G(N) ⊓ N = Z(N) = 1`
(the socle of a primitive group is a product of isomorphic simple groups by Fact 10.2.2
(ii), all of them nonabelian here, so its center is trivial) — a contradiction.

**Checked against the textbook and true as stated.**  Dixon–Mortimer, *Permutation
Groups*, GTM 163, Springer 1996, **Theorem 4.3B**, p. 114, splits a finite primitive `G`
with minimal normal subgroup `K` into (i) `K` regular elementary abelian and
`Soc(G) = K = C_G(K)`; (ii) `K` regular nonabelian, `C_G(K)` a second minimal normal
subgroup and `Soc(G) = K × C_G(K)`; (iii) `K` nonabelian, `C_G(K) = 1`, `Soc(G) = K`.
Case (i) is excluded by the hypothesis that `Soc(G)` is nonabelian.  In case (iii)
`C_G(Soc(G)) = C_G(K) = 1`, and in case (ii)
`C_G(Soc(G)) = C_G(K) ⊓ C_G(C_G(K)) = C_G(K) ⊓ K = 1` because `K` and `C_G(K)` are
independent nonabelian simple factors.  The hypothesis of primitivity cannot be dropped:
for `G = A₅ × ℤ₂` the socle is `A₅ × ℤ₂`, nonabelian, and `C_G(Soc G) = ℤ₂ ≠ 1`.

Proposition 7.2.3, Eq. (41).  *"Let `m₁, m₂, t₁, t₂` be integers; let `m = m₁ + m₂` and
`t = t₁ + t₂`.  Assume `t ≤ m/2` and `tᵢ ≥ 1` for `i = 1,2`.  Then

remaining cases `tᵢ = mᵢ` are Eq. (46); the cases `tᵢ > mᵢ` are trivial, both sides of the

Claim 7.2.4, Eq. (42).  *"Let `1 ≤ k ≤ n - 1`.  Then `C(n,k)² ≤ 4 C(n,k-1) C(n,k+1)`."*

Proof.  *"Expanding and simplifying, the Claim reduces to the statement
`(k+1)/k ≤ 4(n-k)/(n-k+1)`.  This is true because `(k+1)/k ≤ 2` and
`(n-k)/(n-k+1) ≥ 1/2`."*  Cross-multiplied: after multiplying both sides by `k(k+1)` and
using `C(n,k)·k = C(n,k-1)·(n-k+1)` and `C(n,k+1)·(k+1) = C(n,k)·(n-k)`, the claim reduces

decls.name: choose_sub_mul_le
decls.docstring:
The binomial estimate of the proof of Corollary 9.1.3, repaired:
`C(m-r,t)/C(m,t) ≥ 1 - rt/m`, in cross-multiplied form.

The paper's chain is *"`C(m−r,t)/C(m,t) ≥ (1−r/m)^t > 1−(rt/m)`"*.  Its **first step is
false**: for `m = 10`, `r = 1`, `t = 2` it reads `36/45 = 0.8 ≥ 0.81 = (9/10)²`.  In fact
`C(m−r,t)/C(m,t) = ∏_{i<t} (m−r−i)/(m−i) ≤ ((m−r)/m)^t`, the opposite inequality, since
every factor `(m−r−i)/(m−i)` is at most `(m−r)/m`.  The **conclusion** of the chain is
nevertheless true, with `≥` in place of `>`; the strict form is false too, since for `r = 1`
one has `C(m−1,t)/C(m,t) = 1 − t/m` exactly.  See the corrected paper.

Proof (induction on `r`).  For `r = 0` both sides are `m·C(m,t)`.  For the step, write
`A = m − (r+1)t`, `D = m − r − t`; then `m − rt = A + t`, `m − r = D + t` and `A ≤ D`
because `r ≤ rt`, so `A(D+t) ≤ (A+t)D`, i.e.
`(m − (r+1)t)(m − r) ≤ (m − rt)(m − r − t)`.  Multiplying the induction hypothesis by
`m − r − t` and using `C(m−r−1,t)·(m−r) = C(m−r,t)·(m−r−t)`
(`Nat.choose_mul_succ_eq`) gives the claim after cancelling `m − r > 0`.

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Corollary 9.1.3 (PDF p. 71) — The binomial estimate of the proof of Corollary 9.1.3, repaired: `C(m-r,t)/C(m,t) ≥ 1 - rt/m`, in cross-multiplied form.

decls.name: claim_13_2_1_3
decls.docstring:
**§13.2, case (3), the Claim** (Turning local asymmetry into global irregularity).

> Claim (Turning local asymmetry into global irregularity).  In time `m^{O(t)}` we can
> construct a canonical `t`-ary relational structure on `D` with symmetry defect (much)
> greater than `1/2`.
>
> Proof.  We apply Prop. ?? (Local guides). … Thus the assumptions of Prop. ?? are
> satisfied.  The algorithm of Prop. ?? returns canonical `t`-ary relational structures on
> `D_i` with [strong] symmetry defect `≥ |D_i| − t + 1 > m/2`.

The proof is the paper's: build the two categories (`Babai.localGuideData`), check that no
object of `𝓛` is full (`Babai.not_isFullAt_guideMorL`), and apply the Local guide
proposition.  The running time `m^{O(t)}` is
covered inside the RAM proof of Theorem 1.1.1 (`Algo.theorem_1_1_1`) and not stated as a
separate RAM theorem.

decls.name: claim_13_2_1_3_onSet
decls.docstring:
§13.2, **case (3) as a single-string assignment**.

For a finite set `S` of strings, each of which lands in case (3), there is one `t`-ary
relational structure `𝔷(z)` on `D(z)` per `z ∈ S`, with symmetry defect `≥ |D(z)| − t + 1`
and `> m/2`, such that every `G`-isomorphism `z → z'` between members of `S` carries `𝔷(z)`
to `𝔷(z')` along the bijection `D(z) → D(z')` induced by `σ^ϕ`.

This is `Babai.claim_13_2_1_3` with the index family `Subtype.val : ↥S → (Ω → Σ)`; the
point is that the structure depends on the one string `z` and on nothing else, which is
what Sec. 15 line 6 and `Workspace/Master/Bridge.lean` ask for.

decls.name: claim_9_4_step6
decls.docstring:
Claim of step 6 of Procedure Bipartite Split-or-Johnson.  *"Claim.  `X₁` is
uniprimitive.  Proof.  Given that `X₁` is primitive, we only need to rule out that `X₁` is
the clique configuration.  `V₁` is larger than any other color-class in `X`.  Therefore, if
`X₁` were the clique configuration, it would follow by the Large clique lemma
(Lemma 3.4.25) that `V₁` is a twin equivalence class in `X`, a contradiction with the
positive symmetry defect assumption."*  (Version 2.5, lines 4142–4146.)

"`X₁` is the clique configuration" is `rank (X[V₁]) = 2`, so the claim is that the rank of
`X[V₁]` is not `2`; together with the primitivity of `X₁` this is uniprimitivity
(Def. 3.2.1).  The "positive symmetry defect assumption" says that `V₁` is not a single
twin equivalence class of `X`.

decls.name: claim_9_4_step6_general
decls.docstring:
§9.4, the Claim of step 6, **as step 8 re-runs it**: *"`X₁` is uniprimitive."*

The Claim is made of three inputs, which step 6 and step 8 supply from their own data:
`V₁` is one vertex-color class of a coherent configuration `P` and is larger than every
other class (`hmax`), `V₁` is not a single twin equivalence class of `P` (`hdef`, the
positive symmetry defect assumption), and `X₁ = P[V₁]` is primitive (`hprim`, the branch
condition of step 6 for step 6, and the survival of primitivity under the coarsening of
step 8 for step 8).  `h2` is the trivial remark that a configuration on at least two points
has at least two colors.

The content is the Large clique lemma (Lemma 3.4.25), through
`Babai.claim_9_4_step6`: were `X₁` the clique configuration, `V₁` would be a twin
equivalence class of `P`.

Step 8 has to re-run this Claim rather than inherit uniprimitivity from step 6, because a
coarsening of the coloring can lower the rank of `X₁` to `2`; what it cannot do is
disconnect a constituent (`Babai.PartitionStructure.isPrimitive_of_coarser`).

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Lemma 3.4.25 (Large clique lemma) (PDF p. 41) — §9.4, the Claim of step 6, **as step 8 re-runs it**: *"`X₁` is uniprimitive."*

decls.name: claim_9_4_step7
decls.docstring:
Step 7 of Procedure Bipartite Split-or-Johnson.  *"If `X₂` is not homogeneous, let
`(D₁,…,D_k)` be the partition of `V₂` into vertex-color classes.  Pick the smallest `j` such
that the induced bipartite substructure `X[V₁, D_j]` is nontrivial.  (Such a `j` exists
because otherwise `V₁` would be a twin equivalence class in `X₁₂`.)"*
(Version 2.5, lines 4152–4155.)

The content is the parenthesis, stated contrapositively: if *every* `X[V₁, D_j]` is trivial
— for each `j` either no vertex of `V₁` has a neighbor in `D_j`, or every vertex of `V₁` is
joined to every vertex of `D_j` — then all the vertices of `V₁` have the same neighborhood
(the union of the `D_j` of the second kind), hence, `V₁` being a single vertex-color class,
they are pairwise twins, so `V₁` is a twin equivalence class.  That contradicts the standing
assumption that the symmetry defect of `X` on `V₁` is positive.

`D` is the set of vertex-color classes of `V₂`; `hcov` says that they cover `V₂`.

fixes `Ω_j` pointwise when it is the transposition of two points of `Ω_i`, so a twin pair

`Cᵢ ⊆ V₁` such that `|Cᵢ| > n₁/2`.  [Subclaim: `Cᵢ × Bᵢ ⊆ R_j`.]  Now `Y` is not complete

decls.name: claim_9_8
decls.docstring:
Claim of §9.8.  *"Procedure Reduce-by-UPCC makes significant progress.  Specifically,
it either achieves goal (a) or reduces `n₂` by half while maintaining symmetry defect
`≥ 1/2` in each part.  The multiplicative cost is `n₂`."*  (Version 2.5, lines 4333–4336.)

This is the "else" branch: `Y` is the local constituent
`Y = X_m[R_m⁻(x), R_ℓ(x)]` of step 3, which in the notation of §3.4.3 (Def. 3.4.18) is the
`x`-`(m, ℓ, m)`-local constituent for the color `m` *pointing from `V₂` to `V₁`*; so in the
hypotheses below `x ∈ Ωᵢ = V₂`, `R_ℓ(x) ⊆ Ωᵢ = V₂` and `R_m(x) ⊆ Ω_j = V₁`, which is the
paper's `Y⁻` (*"It is nontrivial by Theorem 3.4.19, applied to `Y⁻`"*).

Paper's proof: *"Clearly `Y` is canonical relative to the choice of `x`.  `Y` is
semiregular by Observation 3.4.17.  It is nontrivial by Theorem 3.4.19, applied to `Y⁻`.
We need to verify the assumptions of Theorem 3.4.19.  First we note that both `V₁` and
`V₂` are vertex-color classes in `X`.  Second, we need `n₁/2 < |R_m⁻(x)| < n₁`.  The first
of these inequalities follows because `m` is `α`-dominant and therefore dominant.  The
second inequality is equivalent to the nontriviality of the link `X₁₂`.  Finally, we need
that `X₂` is a UPCC.  (Primitivity guarantees that there are no `X_m`-twins in `V₂`; and we
need "uni" (not a clique) to guarantee that a non-dominant off-diagonal color `ℓ` exists in
`X₂`.)  Summarizing, `Y` is a nontrivial semiregular bipartite graph; therefore its
symmetry defect is `≥ 1/2` (Prop. 2.4.30)."*

The two inequalities `n₁/2 < |R_m(x)| < n₁` are hypotheses here, as in Theorem 3.4.19;
the paper derives them from the dominance of `m` and from the nontriviality of the link.

*"`X₂` is a UPCC"* is `huni`: primitivity is what Theorem 3.4.19 needs, and *"uni"* is what
guarantees that the non-dominant off-diagonal color `ℓ` of step 3 exists.  The
non-dominance of `ℓ` is `hlnd`, and it is what halves `n₂`: `V₂` is replaced by `R_ℓ(x)`.

*The halving is `2|R_ℓ(x)| ≤ n₂`, not `<`.*  Step 3 of the procedure writes
*"`|R_ℓ(x)| < n₂/2`"*, but non-dominance of `ℓ` gives only `|R_ℓ| ≤ n₂²/2`, hence
`|R_ℓ(x)| = |R_ℓ|/n₂ ≤ n₂/2`; nothing in §9.8 excludes equality.  The Claim itself —
*"reduces `n₂` by half"*, and `n₂` significantly reduced in the sense of §9.5 — needs only
`≤`.  See the entry for the Claim of §9.8 in the corrected paper.

decls.name: cor_7_2_2
decls.docstring:
Corollary 7.2.2.  *"Let `α < 1` and `t ≥ 2`.  Then any `α`-coloring of `Γ` (every color
class has size `≤ α|Γ|`) induces a `max(2/3, α)`-coloring of `(Γ choose t)`."*

The statement needs `t ≠ m`, and nothing more.  At `t = m` it is false: `Φ = {Γ}` has one
color class, of relative size `1 > max(2/3, α)` (`cor_7_2_2_false_at_t_eq_m`).  For every
other `t` it holds (see the corrected paper 7.2.1 and Corollary 7.2.2):

* `2t ≤ m`: the paper's proof, `cor_7_2_2_of_two_mul_le`;
* `m/2 < t < m`: complementation `T ↦ Γ ∖ T` carries the color classes of `(Γ choose t)`
 to those of `(Γ choose m-t)` with the same sizes (`card_tupleClass_compl`), and
 `1 ≤ m - t < m/2`, so the first case applies to `m - t`;
* `t > m`: `Φ` is empty.

links.rationale: Formalizes Corollary 7.2.2 (PDF p. 63) — Corollary 7.2.2.  *"Let `α < 1` and `t ≥ 2`.  Then any `α`-coloring of `Γ` (every color class has size `≤ α|Γ|`) induces a `max(2/3, α)`-coloring of `(Γ choose t)`."*

decls.name: cor_7_2_2_false_at_t_eq_m
decls.docstring:
Corollary 7.2.2 is false at `t = m`: on `Γ = {0, 1}` with two colors of size `1` (an
`α`-coloring for `α = 1/2`) and `t = 2`, the only `2`-subset forms a color class of
relative size `1 > max(2/3, 1/2)`.

links.rationale: Formalizes Corollary 7.2.2 (PDF p. 63) — Corollary 7.2.2 is false at `t = m`: on `Γ = {0, 1}` with two colors of size `1` (an `α`-coloring for `α = 1/2`) and `t = 2`, the only `2`-subset forms a color class of relative size `1 > max(2/3, 1/2)`.

decls.name: corollary_10_3_7
decls.docstring:
**Corollary 10.3.7** (Affected Orbit Lemma), §10.3.

> Let `G ≤ S(Ω)` be a permutation group and `ϕ : G → S_k` a giant representation.  Assume
> `k ≥ 5`.  Then, if `∆` is an affected `G`-orbit, i.e. `∆ ∩ D = ∅`, then `ker(ϕ)` is not
> transitive on `∆`; in fact, each orbit of `ker(ϕ)` in `∆` has length `≤ |∆|/k`.

Proof (the paper's): "For `k ≥ 5`, the largest proper subgroup of `A_k` has index `k`, and
the largest subgroup of `S_k` not containing `A_k` also has index `k`.  So the statement
follows from Prop. 10.3.6."  (The index fact is
`Babai.card_le_relIndex_of_not_alternating_le`.)

links.rationale: Formalizes Theorem 1.2.1 (PDF p. 13) — **Corollary 10.3.7** (Affected Orbit Lemma), §10.3.

decls.name: costJh_resolution
decls.docstring:
§11.4, the resolution of item **(v)**.

> (iv) `T_Jh(x) = T_Jh(x,x)`
> (v) `T_Jh(x,y) ≤ q₁(x) (T(4x/5) + T_Jh(x, 0.9y))`
> where `q₁(x)` is a quasipolynomial function.  An upper bound of the form
> `T_Jh(x,y) ≤ T(4x/5) q₁(x)^{O(log y)}` follows, hence Eq. (65) with
> `q(x) = q₁(x)^{O(log x)}`.

Here `f y = T_Jh(x,y)` for a fixed `x`, `A = T(4x/5)` and `c = q₁(x)`; "For
`y < max{5, ℓ(x)}` we set `T(x,y) = 0`" is `hbase` with `y₀ = max{5, ℓ(x)}`.  The bound
obtained is `T_Jh(x,y) ≤ n c^n A` for `y < y₀ (10/9)^n`, and the least such `n` is
`O(log y)`.

decls.name: cost_66
decls.docstring:
§11.4, **Eq. (66)**.

> Our contribution is an inequality of the form `T_Jh(x) ≤ q(x) T(4x/5)`  (65)
> where `q(x)` is a quasipolynomial function.  Combining with item (iii) we obtain
> `T(x) ≤ 2x q(x) T(4x/5) < q(x)² T(4x/5)`.  (66)

The strict inequality needs `2x < q(x)` and `T(4x/5) > 0`, which the paper leaves implicit
(`q` is quasipolynomial, hence eventually larger than `2x`).

decls.name: cost_72
decls.docstring:
§14.2, **Eq. (72)**.

> If `(∀i)(|Ω_i| ≤ 2n/3)` then this yields (generously) the inequality
> `T(G,ϕ) ≤ m · q(m) · T(2n/3)`  (72)
> justifying Inequality (65).

Stated as an inequality about an abstract cost function `T` (as in
`Workspace/Luks/Cost.lean`, where the recurrences of Sec. 11.4 are resolved): from
Eq. (71), `T(G,ϕ) ≤ q(m) ∑_{i<s} T(|Ω_i|)`, and the three-bin bound
`∑_i T(|Ω_i|) ≤ 3 T(2n/3) ≤ m T(2n/3)` for `m ≥ 3`
(`Babai.sum_le_three_mul`).

The step needs no bound on the *number* `s` of color classes — there is none available,
since the classes are indexed by the color vectors of Lemma 7.2.1.  What it needs is that
`T` is monotone and **superadditive** on the range of the sizes: the classes `Ω_i` are
nonempty, so every size is at least `1`, and superadditivity is asked only on `[1, ∞)`.
See `Babai.superadditive_mul_expLogPow` for the paper's quasipolynomial bounds, and
the corrected paper.

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Lemma 7.2.1 (PDF p. 62) — §14.2, **Eq. (72)**.

decls.name: cost_73
decls.docstring:
§14.2, **Eq. (73)**.

> If `(∃i)(|Ω_i| > 2n/3)` then by Lemma 7.2.1, for this `i = i₀` we must have
> `Ω_{i₀} = Ω(Δ_j)` where `|Δ_j| > 2m/3`.  The total contribution of all other `Ω_i` to the
> right-hand side of Eq. (71) is at most `q(m)T(n/3)`. … So in each case we obtain the
> inequality `T(G,ϕ) ≤ q(m)(T(n/3) + T_Jh(n, m/2))`  (73)
> justifying Eq. (v) in Sec. 11.4.

The exceptional class contributes `T_Jh(n, m/2)` — the recursive call on the window
`Ω(Δ_j)` with the reduced `Γ*`, whose size is at most `m/2` by
`Babai.Align_equipartition_card` and `Babai.Align_johnson_card`.  The remaining classes
have total size at most `n/3` (their union is the complement of `Ω_{i₀}`, which has more
than `2n/3` points), and superadditivity turns the sum of their terms into the single term
`T(n/3)` (`Babai.sum_le_of_sum_le`) — again, no bound on their *number* is available or
needed.  As in `Babai.cost_72`, the classes are nonempty and superadditivity is asked only
on `[1, ∞)`.  See the corrected paper.

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Lemma 7.2.1 (PDF p. 62) — §14.2, **Eq. (73)**.

decls.name: cost_le_six_rpow
decls.docstring:
The bound of Corollary 9.1.3 is at most `6^{m/6}` when `t ≥ 2` and `ε ≤ 1/3`.

decls.name: cost_resolution
decls.docstring:
§11.4, the resolution of Eq. (66):

> `T(x) ≤ 2x q(x) T(4x/5) < q(x)² T(4x/5)`  (66)
> which resolves to `T(x) = q(x)^{O(log x)}`, yielding the desired quasipolynomial bound
> on `T(x)`.

Precisely: if `T(x) ≤ 1` below the threshold `x₀` and `T(x) ≤ q(x)² T(4x/5)` above it,
then `T(x) ≤ q(x)^{2n}` as soon as `x < x₀ (5/4)^n`.  Since the least such `n` is
`O(log x)` (`Babai.cost_resolution_log`), this is `T(x) = q(x)^{O(log x)}`.

decls.name: countCalls_le
decls.docstring:
The recursion tree of `Babai.solveFuel` has at most `T I` nodes.

The hypotheses are the ones Sec. 15 supplies for **one round**, all at the true oracle:
`horacle` says the recursion is correct once the fuel exceeds the measure (this is
`Babai.MasterStep.solve_eq_answer`), `hrank` that every call of a round has smaller
measure, `hclosed` that an invariant `P` is inherited by the calls (the invariant is what
lets the recurrence use a bound such as "the window size is at most that of the original
instance"), and `hrec` the one-round recurrence itself.

*Proof.*  Induction on the fuel.  With fuel `f + 1` and `μ I < f + 1`, every call of the
round has measure `< μ I ≤ f`, so the recursion below answers it correctly (`horacle`) and
therefore the round asks exactly the instances it asks under the true oracle
(`Babai.SIReduction.callsWith_eq_calls_of_agree`).  The count is then the number of those
calls plus the counts of their subtrees, which by the induction hypothesis are at most
`T (μ J)`, and the recurrence bounds the sum by `T (μ I)`.

links.rationale: The recursion tree of `Babai.solveFuel` has at most `T I` nodes.

§2.2.2.  "`degtrans(A_n) = n - 2`."

The hypothesis `n ≠ 1` repairs the paper's formula, which is false at `n = 1`

decls.name: degtrans_le_five
decls.docstring:
**Theorem 2.2.4 (a)** (Degree of transitivity), §2.2.2.

Quoted from the paper:

> **Theorem 2.2.4** (Degree of transitivity).  Let `G ≤ S_n` be `t`-transitive.  Assume
> `G` is not a giant.  Then
> (a) (Curtis, Kantor, Seitz [CuKS])  `t ≤ 5`.

Immediately after Theorem 2.2.5 the paper adds: "These results depend on the
Classification of Finite Simple Groups (CFSG)."  The paper gives no proof.

**Citation.** `[CuKS]` = Charles W. Curtis, William M. Kantor, and Gary M. Seitz: *The
2-transitive permutation representations of the finite Chevalley groups*, Trans. Amer.
Math. Soc. **218** (1976), 1–59.  The paper gives no theorem number.

**Used where.** Sec. 13.2 (AggregateCertificates, Theorem 13.2.1), item 2b: "(: so
`1 ≤ d ≤ 5` by Theorem 2.2.4 :)", to bound the number of individualized points by
`d - 1 ≤ 4`.  This is the only use of Theorems 2.2.4 and 2.2.5 in a proof or algorithm of
version 2.5.

**Warning (consistency).** The consistency of this axiom depends on `t`-transitivity being
the paper's notion, `Babai.IsMultiplyTransitive`, which is "the induced action on ordered
`t`-tuples of distinct elements is transitive" with the paper's "transitive" = *exactly one
orbit*.  In particular it forces `t ≤ |Ω|` (`Babai.le_card_of_multiplyTransitive`).  With
Mathlib's `MulAction.IsMultiplyPretransitive` instead, which is vacuously true whenever
`t > |Ω|`, the statement would be **false**: the trivial group on `3` points is not a
giant and would be `6`-transitive.  See the test section at the end of this file.  So this
axiom must never be restated in terms of `IsMultiplyPretransitive`.

links.rationale: Formalizes Theorem 2.2.4 (Degree of transitivity) (PDF p. 17) — **Theorem 2.2.4 (a)** (Degree of transitivity), §2.2.2.
Formalizes Remark 16.1.1 (PDF p. 116) — **Theorem 2.2.4 (a)** (Degree of transitivity), §2.2.2.

decls.name: descentThreshold
decls.docstring:
§11.3, step 6: **the absolute constant of Theorem 11.2.1**, chosen once and for all.

It is the *"`n` greater than some absolute constant"* of Theorem 11.2.1; here it is a
threshold on the number `m` of blocks, which is the size of the permutation domain the
theorem is applied to.

**One constant for all ground sets.**  The binder of the ground set is *inside*
`Babai.Theorem_11_2_1`, which is applied at the type `↥b.ℬ` of blocks, so the constant does
not change with the ground set; see the corrected paper entry on Sec. 11.3 step 6.  It
does carry the universe level of the ground set, as `Babai.c923` and the `c₁` of
`Babai.Theorem_1_1_1_math` do, and for the same reason: the cited result is stated for one
universe level.  What matters for *"absolute"* is the binder order, and the constant is
fixed before the ground set, the alphabet, the group and the strings.

The constant is the maximum of the threshold of Theorem 11.2.1 and of the threshold
`max 25 n₁` under which the machine recognizes a Cameron group (`n₁` from
Prop. 11.2.5). Both are absolute constants, and the paper's *"`n₀`"* only has to be large
enough. With one constant, the instances where step 6 applies are the same for the
mathematical round and for the machine (`Babai.cameronThreshold_le_descentThreshold`).

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Theorem 11.2.1 (PDF p. 93) — §11.3, step 6: **the absolute constant of Theorem 11.2.1**, chosen once and for all.

decls.name: descent_of_cover
decls.docstring:
§11.1, **Proposition 11.1.6** (Descent).

> Let `H ≤ G`.  Then finding `Iso^Δ_G(x,y)` reduces to `|G : H|` instances of finding
> `Iso^Δ_H(x, y^σ)` for various `σ ∈ G`.
>
> *Proof.* We can write `G = ⋃_σ Hσ` where `σ` ranges over a set of right coset
> representatives of `H` in `G`.  Applying Eq. (61) to this decomposition, we obtain
> `Iso^Δ_G(x,y) = ⋃_σ Iso^Δ_{Hσ}(x,y) = ⋃_σ Iso^Δ_H(x, y^{σ⁻¹})σ`  (62)
> where we also employed the shift identity, Eq. (59).

This is Eq. (62) for an arbitrary decomposition `G = ⋃_{σ ∈ R} Hσ` into right cosets.
The number of instances is `|R|`; for the canonical representatives it is exactly
`|G : H|` (`Babai.Proposition_11_1_6_descent`).

decls.name: designLemma_finds_designInputs
decls.docstring:
**Theorem 8.1.2 (Design Lemma) as a reduction at a multiplicative cost**, §8.1 read
through §6.

*"Let `1/2 ≤ α < 1` be a threshold parameter.  Let `X = (Ω, R)` be a `k`-ary relational
structure with `n = |Ω|` vertices, `2 ≤ k ≤ n/2`, and symmetry defect `≥ 1 − α`.  Then in
time `n^{O(k)}` we can find a value `ℓ ≤ k − 1` and a string `x⃗ = x₁ … x_ℓ ∈ Ω^⟨ℓ⟩` of `ℓ`
distinct vertices such that by individualizing each `x_j` we obtain either (a) a canonical
coloring of `Ω` with no dominant color, or (b) a canonical coloring of `Ω` and a
nontrivial canonical equipartition of the dominant color class, or (c) a canonical
coloring of `Ω` and a canonically embedded uniprimitive coherent configuration (UPCC)
whose vertex set is the dominant color class.  Canonicity in the above statements is
relative to `x⃗`."*

The family of "versions" of the input (Def. 6.0.1) is the family of admissible strings
at which Procedure "Design Lemma" returns; the multiplicative cost is their number, at
most `n^k` (`Babai.designOut_ncard_le`).  The outcome at a string is
`Babai.designOutcome`, a function of the input and the string with no choice, and it is
one of (a), (b), (c) (`Babai.designOut_good`).  *"Canonicity relative to `x⃗`"* is
condition (ii) of Definition 6.0.1, `Babai.designOut_equiv`.

The running-time clause *"in time `n^{O(k)}`"* is a separate, pending matter; see
the corrected paper.

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Definition 6.0.1 (Category of tuples) (PDF p. 59) — **Theorem 8.1.2 (Design Lemma) as a reduction at a multiplicative cost**, §8.1 read through §6.

decls.name: dixonMortimer_5_2A
decls.docstring:
**[DiM, Thm. 5.2A]** (Dixon–Mortimer, *Permutation Groups*, GTM 163, Springer 1996,
p. 147), cited by Babai's Theorem 10.4.2, §10.4.  It was an axiom
(`Workspace/Cited/AltQuotients.lean`, `CITED.md` C12); it is now proved along the source
(`Babai.DM52.statement52A`), with the same statement.

Quoted from the source:

> **Theorem 5.2A.** Let `A := Alt(Ω)` where `n := |Ω| ≥ 5`, and let `r` be an integer with
> `1 ≤ r ≤ n/2`.  Suppose that `G ≤ A` has index `|A : G| < (n choose r)`.  Then one of the
> following holds:
> (i) for some `Δ ⊆ Ω` with `|Δ| < r` we have `A_(Δ) ≤ G ≤ A_{Δ}`;
> (ii) `n = 2m` is even, `G` is imprimitive with two blocks of size `m`, and
> `|A : G| = (1/2)(n choose m)`; or
> (iii) one of six exceptional cases hold where:
> (a) `G` is imprimitive on `Ω` and `(n, r, |A : G|) = (6,3,15)`;
> (b) `G` is primitive on `Ω` and `(n, r, |A : G|, G) = (5,2,6,5:2)`, `(6,2,6,PSL₂(5))`,
> `(7,2,15,PSL₃(2))`, `(8,2,15,AGL₃(2))`, or `(9,4,120,PΓL₂(8))`.
>
> **Remark.** […] In part (iii) of the theorem, the groups are listed only with the minimum
> `r` for which they satisfy the hypotheses of the theorem.

So clause (iii) reads "`r` is at least the listed `r`" (see the note on [DiM, Thm. 5.2A,B]
in `Workspace/Cited/AltQuotients.lean`, which also explains the notation).

decls.name: dixonMortimer_5_2B
decls.docstring:
**[DiM, Thm. 5.2B]** (Dixon–Mortimer, *Permutation Groups*, GTM 163, Springer 1996,
pp. 150–151), cited by Babai's Theorem 10.4.2, §10.4.  It was an axiom
(`Workspace/Cited/AltQuotients.lean`, `CITED.md` C12); it is now proved from
Theorem 5.2A along the route the source indicates (`Babai.DM52.statement52B`), with the same
statement.

Quoted from the source:

> **Theorem 5.2B.** Let `S := Sym(Ω)` and `A := Alt(Ω)` where `n := |Ω| ≥ 5`, and let `r`
> be an integer with `1 ≤ r ≤ n/2`.  Suppose that `G ≤ S` has index `|S : G| < (n choose
> r)`.  Then one of the following holds:
> (i) for some `Δ ⊆ Ω` with `|Δ| < r` we have `A_(Δ) ≤ G ≤ S_{Δ}`;
> (ii) `n = 2m` is even, `G` is imprimitive with two blocks of size `m`, and
> `|S : G| = (1/2)(n choose m)`; or
> (iii) one of six exceptional cases hold where:
> (a) `G` is imprimitive with blocks of size 2 on `Ω` and `(n, r, |S : G|) = (6,3,15)`;
> (b) `G` is primitive on `Ω` and `(n, r, |S : G|, G) = (5,2,6,5:4)`, `(6,2,6,PGL₂(5))`,
> `(6,2,12,PSL₂(5))`, `(7,3,30,PSL₃(2))`, or `(8,3,30,AGL₃(2))`.
>
> **Remark.** In part (iii) of the theorem, the groups are listed only with the minimum `r`
> for which they satisfy the hypotheses of the theorem.

So clause (iii) reads "`r` is at least the listed `r`" (see the note on [DiM, Thm. 5.2A,B]
in `Workspace/Cited/AltQuotients.lean`, which also explains the notation).

decls.name: eq_one_of_commute_alternating
decls.docstring:
**The centralizer of `A(Γ)` in `S(Γ)` is trivial** for `|Γ| ≥ 4`.

This is the second half of the group-theoretic step behind
`Babai.AlignDominant.pointwiseStab_orbit_le_ker`; the paper uses it as common knowledge.

*Proof.*  Suppose `q ≠ 1` commutes with every even permutation, and let `y = q(x) ≠ x`.
Pick `z, w` outside `{x, y}` and distinct (there is room, because `|Γ| ≥ 4`), and let
`a = (y z w)` be the corresponding `3`-cycle, an even permutation fixing `x`.  Applying
`q ∘ a = a ∘ q` to `x` gives `q(x) = a(q(x))`, that is, `y = a(y) = z`, contradicting
`z ∉ {x, y}`.

links.rationale: **The centralizer of `A(Γ)` in `S(Γ)` is trivial** for `|Γ| ≥ 4`.

kernel of the sign), hence is trivial; so `Q` centralizes `A(Γ)` and
`Babai.eq_one_of_commute_alternating` makes every `q` trivial.

decls.name: exists_canonicalVersions_9_2_3
decls.docstring:
§15, **line 4c**: *"apply Extended Design Lemma (Theorem 9.2.3)"*, as the canonical
versions of the structure found.

For every string `z` whose hypergraph has a large enough symmetry defect, the algorithm
finds a set `Vers z` of at most `q(m)m^{O(t)}` structures on `Γ` — the multiplicative cost
of Theorem 9.2.3 — each of them a colored `α`-partition of `Γ` or a Johnson scheme on a
subset of `Γ` of at least `αm` vertices (`Babai.IsSplitOutcome`), and the assignment is
canonical: a `G`-shift of the string shifts the whole set of versions by the corresponding
permutation of `Γ` (`Babai.IsCanonicalVersions`).  Strings with a small defect, which line
4b has taken care of, get no version at all.

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Theorem 9.2.3 (Extended Design Lemma) (PDF p. 72) — §15, **line 4c**: *"apply Extended Design Lemma (Theorem 9.2.3)"*, as the canonical versions of the structure found.

decls.name: exists_canonicalVersions_case2b
decls.docstring:
§15, **line 6a at outcome (2b) of Theorem 13.2.1**: the canonical versions of what
Theorem 9.2.3 finds on the family of individualized constituents, read on all of `Γ`.

For every string `z` whose own aggregate is in case (2b), the algorithm finds a non-empty set of
at most `m^5·q(m)m^{O(t)}` outcomes on `Γ` — the `m^{d−1}(m−1) ≤ m^5` individualizations of
case (2b) times the multiplicative cost of Theorem 9.2.3 on each — each of them a colored
`β`-partition of `Γ` or a Johnson scheme on a subset of `Γ` with at least `βm` vertices, for
a `β` that Procedure Align accepts (`1/2 < β`, `5β ≤ 4`).  The assignment is canonical: a
`G`-shift of the string shifts the whole set of versions by the corresponding permutation of
`Γ`, with no claim about which version goes to which, which is exactly what the paper's
*"Warning: the numbering of the `R_i` is not canonical"* allows.

The case test is `Case2 (bigFGamma ϕ z ts) ∧ ¬ AggregateCase2a ϕ z ts`.
Versions are empty off this test, and the same cost bound holds for every string.
The default object of `case2bStr` is chosen from the family at `x`. It is used only
outside `Case2bOk`, so no member of an admissible string's family uses it.

The two thresholds are `βJ = 11/20` for a Johnson scheme inside `C ∖ S` and `βP = 3/4` for a
colored partition of `C ∖ S` extended by `Γ ∖ (C ∖ S)`; both are reached because
`|C ∖ S| ≥ |C| − 4 > 4m/5 − 4 ≥ (11/15)m` for `m ≥ 217`.  See
`Babai.isSplitOutcome_extendOutcome_of`.

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Theorem 9.2.3 (Extended Design Lemma) (PDF p. 72) — §15, **line 6a at outcome (2b) of Theorem 13.2.1**: the canonical versions of what Theorem 9.2.3 finds on the family of individualized constituents, read on all of `Γ`.

decls.name: exists_canonicalVersions_case3
decls.docstring:
§15, **line 6a at outcome (3) of Theorem 13.2.1**: the canonical versions of what
Theorem 9.2.3 finds, read on all of `Γ`.

For every string `z` in the union of the `G`-orbits of the two inputs, the algorithm finds a
set of at most `q(m)m^{O(t)}` outcomes on `Γ` — the multiplicative cost of Theorem 9.2.3 —
each of them a colored `β`-partition of `Γ` or a Johnson scheme on a subset of `Γ` with at
least `βm` vertices, for a `β` that Procedure Align accepts (`1/2 < β`, `5β ≤ 4`).  The
assignment is canonical: a `G`-shift of the string shifts the whole set of versions by the
corresponding permutation of `Γ`.

The `β` depends on which summand the outcome lands in: `3/4` for a colored partition of
`D(z)` extended by `Γ ∖ D(z)`, and `(4/5)·(3/4) = 3/5` for a Johnson scheme inside `D(z)`.
See `Babai.isSplitOutcome_extendOutcome`.

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Theorem 9.2.3 (Extended Design Lemma) (PDF p. 72) — §15, **line 6a at outcome (3) of Theorem 13.2.1**: the canonical versions of what Theorem 9.2.3 finds, read on all of `Γ`.

decls.name: exists_canonicalVersions_family_on
decls.docstring:
**Sec. 14.2, the versions of a canonical reduction applied to a canonical family.**

The input is not one object per string but a finite **family** `Fam z ⊆ ι` of members, each
carrying an object `Str r` of the input category, with

* `Fam (z^σ) = (ϕσ)·Fam z` — the family moves as a *set*, which is what the paper's
 *"Warning: the numbering of the `R_i` is not canonical; isomorphisms may permute the
 `R_i`"* allows, and
* `Str (mv π r) = (Str r)^π` for every member — spelled out, as `Babai.IsCanonicalObj` does,
 as *"the underlying set moves by `π`, and `π` is a morphism"*.

The versions of `z` are the versions of all the members together.  The two multiplicative
costs multiply: at most `V` members, at most `c₀` versions each.

This is the family form of `Babai.exists_canonicalVersions_on`, which is the case of a
one-member family.

The outcomes of `Babai.FindsAtMultCost`, over all individualizations, form a canonical tuple
of structures in the sense `Workspace/Master/Bridge.lean` needs, with the multiplicative cost
of the reduction as the bound on the size of the tuple:

decls.name: exists_conj_perm_of_socle_factors
decls.docstring:
Background for Lemma 10.2.5, Case 2: in a direct product of *nonabelian* simple
groups, the factors are exactly the minimal normal subgroups of the product, so any
automorphism of the product — in particular conjugation by an element of the ambient group
`G`, which normalizes the socle — permutes them.

Proof (elementary): for `N = R₁ × ⋯ × R_s` with all `Rᵢ` nonabelian simple, a normal
subgroup `M ⊴ N` satisfies `[M, Rᵢ] ≤ M ∩ Rᵢ ∈ {1, Rᵢ}` for each `i`, and `[M, Rᵢ] = 1`
for every `i` would force `M ≤ Z(N) = 1`; hence `M` is a subproduct, the minimal normal
subgroups of `N` are precisely `R₁, …, R_s`, and conjugation permutes them.

**Checked against the textbook and true as stated.**  This is Dixon–Mortimer,
*Permutation Groups*, GTM 163, Springer 1996, **Theorem 4.3A (iv)**, p. 112: "If the
subgroups `Kᵢ` in (ii) are all nonabelian, then `K₁, …, K_m` are the only minimal normal
subgroups of `G`" (with Theorem 4.3A (iii) and Corollary 4.3A, p. 113, for `Z(Kᵢ) = 1`).
Applied here to `N = Soc(G)`: each `Rᵢ` is minimal normal in `N` (it is normal in `N` and
simple), the `Rᵢ` are pairwise distinct (`iSupIndep` plus nontriviality), so by 4.3A (iv)
they are *all* the minimal normal subgroups of `N`; `Soc(G)` is characteristic in `G`, so
conjugation by `g ∈ G` restricts to an automorphism of `N` and therefore permutes them.
The permutation `π` is well defined and bijective because the `Rᵢ` are distinct.

decls.name: exists_mem_setwiseStab_map_eq_of_unaffected
decls.docstring:
**The shared first step of case 3** (the corrected paper. 14.1–14.2, Procedure Align,
"Smallest change", item 3): *"a point of `B_T` can be unaffected only if the stabilizer of
`T` in `Aut(Y)` maps onto a group containing `A(Γ*)`"*.

If `u` is unaffected by `ϕ* = ψ ∘ ϕ|_{G*}` then every `π ∈ A(Γ*)` is `ψ(h)` for some
`h ∈ H` that stabilizes the label `T(u)` setwise.

*Proof.*  Unaffected means `A(Γ*) ≤ ϕ*(G*_u)`, so `π = ϕ*(σ) = ψ(ϕ(σ))` for some

decls.name: exists_minimalSystemOfImprimitivity
decls.docstring:
§11.3, Procedure Reduce-to-Johnson, **step 4**: "Find minimal block system `ℬ`."

For a transitive group on at least two points there is a minimal system of imprimitivity
(a system with at least two blocks whose blocks are maximal): start from the system of
singletons and take a system whose blocks are maximal among the proper blocks of
imprimitivity, which exists because `Ω` is finite.

In detail: `{u}` is a block of imprimitivity that is not all of `Ω` (here `|Ω| ≥ 2` is
used), so among the blocks of imprimitivity containing `u` and different from `Ω` there is
a maximal one, `B`.  The system is `ℬ = {B^σ | σ ∈ G}`; transitivity makes it cover `Ω`
and makes `G` transitive on it, and `B ≠ Ω` gives a second block.  A block `C ⊇ B^σ` is
carried by `σ⁻¹` to a block containing `B`, so by maximality it is `B` or `Ω`, i.e.
`C = B^σ` or `C = Ω`.

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Procedure Reduce-to-Johnson (PDF p. 94) — §11.3, Procedure Reduce-to-Johnson, **step 4**: "Find minimal block system `ℬ`."

decls.docstring:
The combinatorial step of Proposition 9.1.1 (§9.1).  Let `Π` be an admissible colored
partition of a finite set `V`, invariant under a group `H ≤ S(V)`, and let `Y ⊆ V` be an
`H`-invariant set on which `H` acts transitively and primitively, with `|Y| ≥ 2` and
`2|Y| > |V|`.  Then some block of `Π` is at least as large as `Y`.

Proof.  Fix `y₀ ∈ Y`.  The set `B = B(y₀) ∩ Y` is nonempty, contained in `Y`, and is a
block of imprimitivity for `H` on `Y`: for `σ ∈ H` the image `σ(B)` is `B(σy₀) ∩ Y`, and
two blocks of a partition are equal or disjoint.  By primitivity `B = Y` — which is the
conclusion — or `B = {y₀}`.  In the second case transitivity gives `B(y) ∩ Y = {y}` for
every `y ∈ Y`; all points of `Y` have the same color, so the color class of `y₀` contains
`Y` and has `≥ 2` elements, so admissibility gives `|B(y)| ≥ 2`, so each `B(y)` has a
point outside `Y`.  Different `y` give different points (the blocks are disjoint), so
`|Y| ≤ |V| - |Y|`, against `2|Y| > |V|`.

The hypothesis `hprim` is the paper's primitivity of the action on `Y` (§2.2.1), stated
for the subsets of `Y`: a nonempty block of imprimitivity inside `Y` is `Y` or a
singleton.

original as a comment): the while loop is executed at least once
(`Babai.one_le_haltIndex`), and after the first round `W ⊇ Aff(G_T, ψ_T) ⊇ Ω(T)`, because
every `u` with `∅ ≠ T(u) ⊆ T` is affected by `(G_T, ψ_T)`: by Eq. (52), `G_u^ϕ` stabilizes

`T(u)` is a nonempty proper subset of `T` (proper since the number `(m choose |T(u)|)` of
standard blocks is at most `n < 2^{t-2}`, so `|T(u)| < t`) and `A(T)` is transitive for
`t ≥ 3`.  That `T(u) ≠ ∅` uses Theorem 10.5.1 (b) and (d) together with the transitivity
of `G`: `Ω` is a single orbit, and at least one orbit is affected.

The items (a), (b), (c), (d) of Theorem 10.5.1 are used in the form they take for a
representation with target `S(Γ)` (`Workspace/AltQuotients/GeneralTarget.lean`).

decls.name: fact_10_2_2_ii
decls.docstring:
**Fact 10.2.2 (ii)**, §10.2: "The socle of a primitive permutation group is a direct
product of isomorphic simple groups."

Formerly an axiom citing `[Sco]`, `[AsS]`, `[DiM, Thm. 4.3B]`; the statement is unchanged.
The proof follows Dixon–Mortimer, *Permutation Groups*, GTM 163: by [DiM, Thm. 4.3B] a
primitive group has one minimal normal subgroup `M₁`, or two, `M₁ ≅ M₂`; the socle is `M₁`

decls.docstring:
§9.7.  **The common exit of Cases 2, 3a1, 3a2 and 3b, as a reduction.**

The data are: a category `C` of inputs, each carrying an input of §9.7 (`bbd`) whose
isomorphisms are the isomorphisms of `C` (`hbbd`); a canonical sub-family `Sel Y` of the
blocks (`hSelIso`), which is what Procedure Reduce-Part2-by-Color selects; and a canonical
coloring `Hint Y` of the ordered pairs of the kept blocks (`hHintIso`), which is the
structure found on `Sel Y`.

The conclusion is the reduction that returns the restricted input `X[V₁, Sel Y]` with the
hint.  It is an outcome of §9.7 (`Babai.IsBlkDesignOutcome`) by `hprog`, which is the
disjunction of the two remaining kinds of major progress of §9.5: *"`n₂` is significantly
reduced"* (`10|U| ≤ 9n₂`) or *"`X₂` moves from clique to UPCC while `n₂` does not
increase"* (`|U| ≤ n₂` and the hint).

There is one outcome, so any cost `≥ 1` pays for it.
