decls.name: theorem_10_5_1_a
decls.docstring:
**Theorem 10.5.1 (a)** (Main Structure Theorem), §10.5.

> For every `x ∈ Ω` there exists a unique subset `T(x) ⊂ [k]` such that `|T(x)| < k/4` and
> `(A_k)_(T(x)) ≤ G_x^ϕ ≤ (S_k)_{T(x)}`.  (52)

Proof (the paper's): the Jordan–Liebeck theorem (Thm. 10.4.2) with `K = G^ϕ`,
`H = G_x^ϕ`, `r = ⌊k/4⌋`, using
`(k choose ⌊k/4⌋) > 2^{k/2} ≥ n₀ ≥ |x^G| = |G : G_x| ≥ |G^ϕ : G_x^ϕ|`.  (53)

Since Theorem 10.4.2 is false as printed, the form to use here is
`Babai.theorem_10_4_2_of_four_mul_le`: its hypothesis `4r ≤ k` holds for `r = ⌊k/4⌋`, so
the paper's conclusion is available and item (a) stands exactly as printed.

decls.name: theorem_10_5_1_e_johnson
decls.docstring:
**Theorem 10.5.1 (e)**, §10.5, the namesake conclusion:

> The action of `G` on the set of standard blocks in `Δ` is `A_k^(t_Δ)` or `S_k^(t_Δ)`.

The labelling bijection `e` of `theorem_10_5_1_e_labels` carries the block set onto the
`t_Δ`-subsets of `[k]`; transporting the action `G^ℬ` (`Babai.onBlocks`) along `e` gives
the Johnson group `A_k^(t_Δ)` (`Babai.JohnsonA`) or `S_k^(t_Δ)` (`Babai.JohnsonS`),
according to whether `G^ϕ = A_k` or `G^ϕ = S_k`.  The labelling clause is restated here
membershipwise (`a ∈ label ↔ a ∈ T(y)`) to avoid a `Set.toFinset` decidability side
condition.

decls.name: theorem_10_5_1_g
decls.docstring:
**Theorem 10.5.1 (g)**, §10.5.

> If `Ψ = {C₁, …, C_r}` is another system of imprimitivity on the orbit `∆` such that the
> kernel of the action `G → S(Ψ)` is `ker(ϕ)` then `r = (k choose t')` for some
> `t' < t_Δ` and the `G`-action on `Ψ` is `S_k^(t')` or `A_k^(t')`.  In particular, the
> standard blocks form the unique largest system of imprimitivity on which the kernel of
> `G`-action is `ker(ϕ)`.  Moreover, if `x ∈ Cᵢ` then `|T(G_{Cᵢ})| = t'` and
> `T(G_{Cᵢ}) ⊂ T(x)`.

**"another".**  The paper's word *another* system of imprimitivity means: different from
the system of standard blocks.  Dropping it makes the statement false, because the
standard blocks themselves satisfy the remaining hypotheses (by item (e)) while having
`C(k, t_Δ)` blocks, not `C(k, t')` with `t' < t_Δ`.  So the hypothesis
`hΨne : Ψ ≠ standardBlocks ϕ (orbit G x)` is part of the theorem.  (A formalization
matter, not a correction from the paper.)

**correction: the blocks of `Ψ` must be maximal.**  As printed, (g) is false.  Let `S_k` act
on the ordered triples of distinct elements of `[k]` with `k = 32`, so `n₀ = 29760`,
`2 log₂ n₀ < 30 ≤ k`, `ϕ` is the identification of `G` with `S_k`, `ker ϕ = 1`,
`T(a,b,c) = {a,b,c}` and `t_Δ = 3`.  Let `Ψ` be the partition of the triples by their first
two coordinates.  It is a system of imprimitivity, the action on it is faithful, so its
kernel is `ker ϕ`, and it is not the standard system.  It has `r = 32 · 31 = 992` blocks,
which is none of `C(32,0) = 1`, `C(32,1) = 32`, `C(32,2) = 496`.  (The system of singletons
in the example of Remark 10.5.3 is a second counterexample.)  The paper's proof says
"`H = G_{Cᵢ}` is a maximal subgroup of `G`", which holds exactly when `Cᵢ` is a maximal
block.  So the hypothesis that the proof uses is added to the statement: `Ψ` is a
*minimal system of imprimitivity* in the paper's own term (Sec. 11.1: "systems with at
least two blocks that cannot be made coarser, i. e., the blocks are maximal"),
`Babai.IsMinimalSystemOfImprimitivity`.  See the corrected paper "Theorem 10.5.1 (g):
false unless the blocks of `Ψ` are maximal".

**Proof route.**  The paper's, with one unproved fact derived.  Let `x ∈ Cᵢ` and
`H = G_{Cᵢ}`.  Then `Gₓ ≤ H`, and `H` is a maximal subgroup of `G` because `Cᵢ` is a
maximal block.  The kernel `N = ker ϕ` fixes every block, so `N ≤ H`, and `H^ϕ` is a
maximal subgroup of `G^ϕ` with `|G : H| = |G^ϕ : H^ϕ| = r`.  First `r ≥ 3`, because
`r! ≥ |G : N| ≥ k!/2`.  The paper then quotes: "the only maximal subgroups of `S_k`
containing `(A_k)_(T)` are of the form `(S_k)_U` for `U ⊆ T`".  We get this from results
already in hand: `|G^ϕ : H^ϕ| ≤ |G^ϕ : Gₓ^ϕ| ≤ n₀ < C(k, ⌊k/4⌋)` by Eq. (53), so
Theorem 10.4.2 (form `Babai.theorem_10_4_2_of_four_mul_le`) gives `T' := T(H^ϕ)` with
`(A_k)_(T') ≤ H^ϕ ≤ (S_k)_{T'}`, and Observation 10.4.1 applied to
`(A_k)_(T(x)) ≤ Gₓ^ϕ ≤ H^ϕ ≤ (S_k)_{T'}` gives `T' ⊆ T(x)`.  Since `r ≥ 3`, `T' ≠ ∅`, so
`(G^ϕ)_{T'}` is a proper subgroup of `G^ϕ` containing `H^ϕ`, and maximality gives
`H^ϕ = (G^ϕ)_{T'}`.  Hence `r = C(k, t')` with `t' = |T'|`, and the Johnson action on `Ψ`
follows the lines of item (e).  If `T' = T(x)` then `H^ϕ = (G^ϕ)_{T(x)} = (G_B)^ϕ` for the
standard block `B ∋ x` by item (f), so `H = G_B` (both contain `N`), `Cᵢ = B`, and `Ψ` is
the standard system, contrary to `hΨne`.  So `T' ⊊ T(x)` and `t' < t_Δ`.

decls.name: theorem_10_5_1_g_largest
decls.docstring:
**Theorem 10.5.1 (g)**, §10.5, the "In particular" clause:

> In particular, the standard blocks form the unique largest system of imprimitivity on
> which the kernel of `G`-action is `ker(ϕ)`.

As printed, over *all* systems of imprimitivity, this is false: in the example of
Remark 10.5.3 (`S_k` on ordered pairs, `k = 16`) the system of singletons has trivial
kernel `= ker ϕ` and `240` blocks, more than the `C(16,2) = 120` standard blocks.  It is
the consequence of item (g) as repaired (the corrected paper: `Ψ` is a minimal
system of imprimitivity), so it holds among minimal systems: every minimal system with
kernel `ker ϕ` has at most as many blocks as the standard system, and only the standard
system has that many.  *Proof.*  If `Ψ` is not the standard system, item (g) gives
`|Ψ| = C(k,t')` with `t' < t_Δ`, while there are `C(k,t_Δ)` standard blocks (item (e));
since `4 t_Δ < k` (item (a)), `C(k,t') < C(k,t_Δ)`.

**Theorem 13.1.3** (Local certificates), §13.1.

> Let `T ⊆ Γ` where `|T| = t`.  We refer to `T` as our "test set."  Assume
> `max{8, 2 + log₂ n} < t ≤ m/10`.  By making `≤ t!n²` calls to String Isomorphism

> decide whether `T` is full and
> (a) if `T` is full, find a certificate `K(T) ≤ Aut_G(x)` of fullness;
> (b) if `T` is not full, find a certificate `M(T) ≤ S(T)` of non-fullness.

outputs `K(T)` (`Babai.certK`) and `M(T)` (`Babai.certM`) of Procedure LocalCertificates.

`Workspace/LocalCertificates/Canonicity.lean`.  The `t! poly(n)` running time is
covered inside the RAM proof of Theorem 1.1.1 (`Algo.theorem_1_1_1`) and not stated as a
separate RAM theorem.

decls.name: theorem_13_2_1
decls.docstring:
**Theorem 13.2.1** (AggregateCertificates), §13.2, as one statement.

> Let `ϕ : G → S(Γ)` be a giant representation, where `G ≤ S(Ω)`, `|Ω| = n`, and
> `|Γ| = m`.  Let `max{8, 2 + log₂ n} < t < m/10`.  Then, at a multiplicative cost of
> `m^{O(t)}`, we can either find a canonical colored 4/5-partition of `Γ` or find a
> canonically embedded `t`-ary relational structure with relative symmetry defect `≥ 1/2`
> on `Γ`, or reduce the determination of `Iso_G(x,y)` to `n^{O(1)}` instances of size
> `≤ 2n/3`.

The `cost` of the statement is the multiplicative cost of the *case analysis* (the paper's
`m^{O(t)}` is the number of runs of the two routines of §13.1, `Babai.card_testSets` and
`Babai.card_comparePairs`, which is paid before the case analysis begins and is the same in
all four branches).  Cases (1), (2a) and (3) cost `1`; case (2b) costs
`m^{d−1}(m−1) ≤ m^5` (`Babai.case2b_cost`, `Babai.case2b_cost_le`).

The four outcomes are:

* (1) the colored 4/5-partition `Babai.orbitPartition` of `Γ`, canonical because `F(x)` is
 (`Babai.canonical_bigF`);
* (2a) the hypothesis of Corollary 12.0.10 on the canonical orbit `C`, `|C| > 4m/5`;
* (2b) a canonical subset `C' = C ∖ S` of `Γ` carrying the orbital configuration of
 `F^C_{(S)}`, whose off-diagonal constituents are binary relational structures of relative
 symmetry defect `≥ 1/2` (`Babai.case2b_defect`);
* (3) the set `D` of fixed points of `F^Γ` with `|D| > 4m/5`, on which no test set is full
 (`Babai.disjoint_fixedGamma_of_isFull`), together with the output of the Claim
 (`Babai.claim_13_2_1_3`): for the pair `(x, x')` formed by `x` and any second input `x'`
 whose own set of fixed points is again large (which is what makes the procedure land in
 case (3) for `x'` as well), the canonical `t`-ary relational structures on `D(x)` and
 `D(x')` with symmetry defect `≥ |D| − t + 1 > m/2` (`Babai.IsCase3Output`).

Canonicity of all four outcomes is canonicity of `F(x)`, `Babai.canonical_bigF`: every
`τ ∈ G` carries `F(x^τ)` to `τ⁻¹F(x)τ`, hence `F(x^τ)^Γ` to `(τ^ϕ)⁻¹F(x)^Γτ^ϕ`, and each of
`Babai.orbitPartition`, the orbits `C`, the set `D` and the orbital configuration is built
from `F^Γ` alone.

decls.name: theorem_13_2_1_cases
decls.docstring:
**Theorem 13.2.1** (AggregateCertificates), §13.2, the case distinction.

> (1) if the nontrivial orbits … of `F^Γ` cover at least `m/5` elements of `Γ` and no
> orbit of `F^Γ` has length `> 4m/5` … (2) else if `F^Γ` has an orbit `C ⊆ Γ` of length
> `|C| > 4m/5` … (3) else `|D| ≥ 4m/5` where `D ⊆ Γ` is the set of fixed points of `F^Γ`.

The three cases are exhaustive, with the stronger, strict inequality `4m < 5|D|` in
case (3).  The outcome of each case is:

* case (1): the colored 4/5-partition `Babai.orbitPartition`
 (`Babai.orbitPartition_isAlphaPartition`);
* case (2a): the hypothesis of Corollary 12.0.10
 (`Babai.corollary_12_0_10_hypothesis_of_giant`);
* case (2b): `1 ≤ d ≤ 5` (`Babai.degtrans_restrict_le_five`), the individualization of
 `d − 1` points (`Babai.isTransitive_pointwiseStab_individualize`,
 `Babai.not_isDoublyTransitive_pointwiseStab_individualize`), the orbital configuration
 (`Babai.orbitalConfig_individualize_isCoherent`,
 `Babai.orbitalConfig_individualize_isHomogeneous`, `Babai.three_le_rank_orbitalConfig`)
 and the multiplicative cost `Babai.case2b_cost`;
* case (3): `Babai.claim_13_2_1_3`, via the Local guide proposition.

The multiplicative cost `m^{O(t)}` of the theorem is the number of runs of the two
routines of §13.1: `C(m,t)` runs of LocalCertificates and `2·C(m,t)²` runs of
CompareLocalCertificates (`Babai.card_testSets`, `Babai.card_comparePairs`), times the
`m^{d−1}(m−1)` of case (2b).  The running time proper is the RAM theorem
`Algo.theorem_13_2_1_ram` (`Algo/Agg1321RAM.lean`): `10¹²·Σ τ(W) + (m+1)^{O(t)}·poly(input)`
steps outside the String Isomorphism calls, and at most `Babai.aggregateRoundCost m t n`
calls on windows of at most `n/t` points (`Algo.a13_calls`).

decls.name: theorem_1_2_1_a
decls.docstring:
**Theorem 1.2.1 (a)** (Unaffected Stabilizers Lemma), §1.2.  "Let `G ≤ S(Ω)` be a
permutation group and let `n₀` denote the length of the largest orbit of `G`.  Let
`ϕ : G → S_m` be a giant representation.  Let `U ⊆ Ω` denote the set of elements of `Ω` not
affected by `ϕ`. … Assume `m > max{8, 2 + log₂ n₀}`.  Then `ϕ` maps `G_(U)`, the pointwise
stabilizer of `U`, onto `A_m` or `S_m` (so `ϕ : G_(U) → S_m` is still a giant
representation).  In particular, `U ≠ Ω` (at least one element is affected)."

The first conclusion is Theorem 10.3.5 (`theorem_10_3_5`): a subgroup of `S_m` containing
`A_m` is `A_m` or `S_m`.  For the second: if `U = Ω` then `G_(U) = 1`, so its image is
trivial, while `A_m` is not, since `m ≥ 9`.

decls.name: theorem_9_2_2
decls.docstring:
Theorem 9.2.2 (Bipartite Split-or-Johnson).  *"Let `X = (V₁, V₂; E, f)` be a
vertex-colored bipartite graph with `|V₁| ≥ 2` and let `2/3 ≤ α < 1` be a threshold
parameter.  Assume `|V₂| < α|V₁|`.  Assume moreover that the symmetry defect of `X` on
`V₁` is at least `1 - α`.  Then at quasipolynomial multiplicative cost we can find either
(a) a canonical colored `α`-partition of `V₁`, or (b) a canonically embedded nontrivial
Johnson scheme on a subset of `V₁` of size `≥ α|V₁|`.  (The time bounds do not depend on
`α`.)"*  (Version 2.5, lines 4019–4025.)

The hypotheses on `X` and on `α` are the defining conditions of the input category
`BipInputs Ω`, whose objects carry `α` as data; the conclusion is about `V₁`, so the set
to be split in `IsSplitOutcome` is `BipInputs.V₁ X` and the threshold is
`BipInputs.alpha X`.

*How the printed statement is recovered.*  Fixing `α` means passing to the full
subcategory `BipInputsAt Ω α` of the objects whose threshold is `α`; its morphisms are
exactly the isomorphisms of the underlying vertex-colored bipartite graphs, so it is the
category of the printed statement.  `Babai.FindsAtMultCost.full` restricts the reduction
to it, giving `Babai.theorem_9_2_2_at`, which is the printed statement verbatim.  The
parenthetical *"(The time bounds do not depend on `α`.)"* is the quantifier over `q`
standing outside, here automatically, since `q` does not see `α` at all.

*The cost function is absolute.*  The quantifier over `q` also stands outside the
quantifier over the ambient type `Ω`, so one and the same `q` serves every ground set.
Were `Ω` fixed first, a constant function of `|Ω|` would satisfy the bound and the
statement would say nothing about growth in `n`; see the entry on the absolute constants
in the corrected paper.

*How it is proved.*  The recursion of §9.4-§9.8 runs in the wider category
`Babai.BipBlockInputs`, in which a vertex of `V₂` is a block of points, because step 2(ii)
of Procedure ImprimitiveCase (§9.6) returns the contracted graph, whose second part is a
set of blocks (see `Workspace/SplitOrJohnson/BipBlocks.lean` and the entry for Lemma 9.6.1
in the corrected paper).  The printed statement is the case of singleton blocks, and follows
from `Babai.theorem_9_2_2_blocks` along the canonical embedding `Babai.bipToBlk`, which
keeps the underlying set, `α` and `V₁`.

decls.name: theorem_9_2_3
decls.docstring:
Theorem 9.2.3 (Extended Design Lemma).  *"Let `3/4 ≤ α < 1` be a threshold parameter.
Let `X = (Ω, R)` be a `k`-ary relational structure with `n` vertices, `2 ≤ k ≤ n/4`, and
relative strong symmetry defect `> 1 - α`.  Then at a multiplicative cost of `q(n)n^{O(k)}`,
where `q(n)` is a quasipolynomial function, we can find either (a) a canonical colored
`α`-partition of the vertex set, or (b) a canonically embedded nontrivial Johnson scheme
on a subset `W ⊆ Ω` of size `|W| ≥ αn`.  (The time bounds do not depend on `α`.)"*
(Version 2.5, lines 4029–4035.)

`n^{O(k)}` is `n^(c*k)` for an absolute constant `c`, quantified — like `q` — outside `α`
and `k`, since the bound is uniform.  Both are also quantified outside the ambient type
`Ω`: they are absolute constants, so one pair `(q, c)` serves every ground set.  With `Ω`
fixed first the statement would say nothing, because for a fixed finite `Ω` a constant
function is a quasipolynomial bound on every input; see the entry on the absolute

Theorem 9.2.3 **from the Design Lemma in the form of §6**: given a reduction at
multiplicative cost `n^k` that finds an outcome of Theorem 8.1.2 canonically
(`Babai.DesignOutcomes`, `Babai.IsDesignOutcome`), Theorem 9.2.3 follows.

Theorem 8.1.2 restated as a `Babai.FindsAtMultCost`, namely `Babai.designLemma_finds`.  The chain is: the Design Lemma, a canonical case distinction
on its outcome (outcomes (a) and (b) are a colored `α`-partition of `Ω`; outcome (c) goes
to Theorem 9.2.1 at the threshold `β = αn/|C|`), then the transfer
`Babai.transfer_finds`.  The cost is `n^k · max(1, q(n)) ≤ q'(n)·n^{1·k}` with

decls.docstring:
§9.2, the proof of Theorem 9.2.3: the transfer of a solution for the dominant class
`C` to a solution for the whole vertex set `V`.

This is the transfer clause of Lemma 9.3.1 (`Babai.lemma_9_3_1_transfer`) with the pair of
thresholds `(β, α) = (αn/|C|, α)`, for which the required equality `β|C| = α|V|` is the
definition of `β`.  In objective (a) the extra block is `V \ C`, of size
`|V| − |C| < (1 − α)|V| ≤ α|V|` since `α ≥ 1/2`; in objective (b) the Johnson scheme is
already large enough, since `β|C| = α|V|`.

decls.name: turnConst
decls.docstring:
The absolute constant in the exponent of `Babai.turnCost`.

It has to be large enough for every multiplicative cost that one turn of Procedure
Bipartite Split-or-Johnson can incur.  The largest of them is §9.7, Case 3a: *"Apply the
Design lemma to `H`, viewed as a `d₁`-ary relational structure.  (Multiplicative cost
`n₂^{d₁} < n₂^{(7/3) log₂ n₁}`.)"*, which is `2^{(7/3)(log₂ n)²}` and already exceeds
`2^{(log₂ n + 2)²}`.  The other costs of one turn are §9.6 (`n₂`), §9.8 (`n₂`), the extra
factor `m ≤ n₂/2` of §9.7 Case 3a1, and Procedure Reduce-Part2-by-Color (Lemma 9.3.2);
they are polynomial in `n`, and one turn may incur several of them at once, so the
constant must leave room for a polynomial factor as well.

With the value `4` the exponent is `4(log₂ n + 2)²`, which is `(7/3)(log₂ n + 2)²` for
Case 3a plus a slack of `(5/3)(log₂ n + 2)²`; the slack alone covers `n^k` for every
`k ≤ (5/3)(log₂ n + 2)`, so it covers every polynomial factor of one turn on all but
finitely many `n`, and `Babai.constFactor` covers the rest.

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Lemma 9.3.2 (PDF p. 74) — The absolute constant in the exponent of `Babai.turnCost`.

decls.docstring:
§14.1, **Eq. (70)** for an individualized pair of versions: if `σ ∈ G` carries the fixed
version `X'` of `x` to the version `Y'` of `y`, then

 `Iso_G^{X' ↦ Y'}(x,y) = Iso_{G₁}(x, y^{σ⁻¹})σ`,  `G₁ = ϕ⁻¹(Aut(X'))`.

(The paper's right coset `Kσ` is Lean's left translate `σ • K`.)

X'^{σ^ϕ}` iff `X'^{ρ^ϕ} = X'`, i.e. iff `ρ ∈ G₁`.

decls.name: StepBounds
decls.docstring:
**The explicit costs of one node of the variant round.** All numeric fields are explicit
in tier 2 (closed expressions in the constants of the Cameron routine), existential in tier 1.

* sizes: the fields of `Algo.Round.RunCostQ`, with explicit bounds; the states of a run
 through the invariant (`inv_size`, R4);
* calls: at a good node of degree `n`, the run makes at most `2^{Aw (log₂ n+2)^4}` calls at
 route 1 (line 2, `m ≤ ℓ = (log n)^3`), at most `2^{Ap (log₂ n+2)^3}` elsewhere (R3);
* one DFS step (with the loop counter), on every state satisfying the invariant `Inv n` of
 a run from a root of degree `n`, in time quasipolynomial in `n` and polynomial in the size
 of the state: `2^{As (log₂ n+2)^5}·(size+1)^ds`;
* the polynomial routines around the loop: the entry (normalization and root), `ground`,
 the well-formedness test, `init`, and the read-off.

links.rationale: **The explicit costs of one node of the variant round.** All numeric fields are explicit in tier 2 (closed expressions in the constants of the Cameron routine), existential in tier 1.

* `W`: the wide nodes. At a wide node every call of the run shrinks the window to at most

The potential is `win²·(2(Qw n₀+1))^{windowRank win}·(Qp n₀+1)^{johnsonRankOf win param}`.

decls.name: cleanCompute_recursion
decls.docstring:
**The recursion theorem.**  A recursive procedure is presented by

* `setUp : α → ℕ × σ`, which turns the input into the number of calls the recursion will make
 and the initial state (the stack holding the single top-level call), computed by a clean
 routine `P₁`;
* `step : σ → σ`, one call of the procedure — pop a pending subproblem, do its local work, push
 its subcalls — computed, in the counting form `(k, s) ↦ (k - 1, step s)`, by a clean routine
 `Q`;
* `readOff : σ → β`, which reads the answer off the final state, computed by a clean routine
 `P₃`.

If one call costs at most `p (Enc.size a)` and the recursion makes `(setUp a).1` calls, then the
whole procedure runs in `T₁ n + (q n * (p n + 2) + 1) + u n` steps, where `q` bounds the number
of calls and `u` the cost of reading off the answer.

**Bit growth.**  If every register of the initial configuration holds a value at most `B`,
and every constant, register index and jump target of `P` is at most `B`, then after `k` steps
every register holds a value at most `2 ^ k * B`.

This is the justification of the unit-cost measure: `k` steps of the machine produce numbers of
at most `k + Nat.size B` bits, so each unit-cost step hides at most `O(k + log B)` bit
operations, and unit-cost time is within a polynomial factor of logarithmic-cost time, hence of
Turing machine time.

and `Babai.le_add_two_of_involved_GL` (cited by the paper).

decls.name: cor_9_1_3_strict_stabilizers
decls.docstring:
Corollary 9.1.3.  *"Let `G ≤ Aut(J(m,t))` and `0 < ε ≤ 1/3`.  If `m!/|G| < (t/ε)^{εm/t}`
then `G` acts as a primitive group on a subset of relative size `≥ (1 - ε)`."*
(Version 2.5, lines 3953–3966.)

Paper's proof: *"The condition implies that `|S_m : G| < 1.9^m`.  Let `r` be the smallest
value such that `|S_m : G| < C(m, r+1)`.  By Lemma 9.1.2, we have a Johnson group
`A⁽ᵗ⁾_{m-r} ≤ G⁽ᵗ⁾` act on a subset of size `C(m-r,t)`.  This group is primitive on this
subset.  Now `C(m-r,t)/C(m,t) ≥ (1 - r/m)^t > 1 - (rt/m)`.  So we are done if `rt/m > ε`.
Let us assume `rt/m ≤ ε`.  Then `|S_m : G| ≥ C(m,r) ≥ (m/r)^r = (m/r)^{r/m·m} ≥
(t/ε)^{εm/t}`, contrary assumption."*

Three points about this proof:
* the two occurrences of the condition on `rt/m` are interchanged: the corollary is proved
 when `rt/m ≤ ε` (then the subset has relative size `> 1 - ε`), and the contradiction
 (50) is derived in the case `rt/m > ε`, where `r > εm/t` makes `C(m,r) ≥ (m/r)^r`
 exceed `(t/ε)^{εm/t}` — with the inequality as printed the chain (50) runs the wrong
 way, since `u ↦ (1/u)^u` is increasing on `(0, 1/e)` and `ε/t ≤ 1/3 < 1/e`;
* the displayed chain `C(m−r,t)/C(m,t) ≥ (1−r/m)^t > 1−(rt/m)` is false in both steps
 (`m = 10`, `r = 1`, `t = 2` gives `0.8 ≥ 0.81`; and `r = 1` gives equality in the second
 step).  Its conclusion holds with `≥`, and that is what is used; the repaired step is
 `Babai.choose_sub_mul_le` above;
* the alternative (ii) of the repaired Lemma 9.1.2 is excluded here by the index bound:
 in that case `|S_m : G| = C(m, ⌊m/2⌋)/2`, which exceeds `(t/ε)^{εm/t} ≤ 1.4447^m` for
 `m ≥ 6`.

The subset of relative size `≥ 1 - ε` is a subset of the **vertex set of the Johnson
scheme**, i.e. of the `t`-subsets: it is the set of `t`-subsets of `Γ = [m] \ T`, of size
`C(m-r,t) ≥ (1-ε)C(m,t)`.

The upper bound `G ≤ S(Γ)_T` from Lemma 9.1.2 makes `Δ = Tᶜ` invariant under `G`.
Thus `G` acts on the `t`-subsets of `Δ`. Its induced group contains `A(Δ)` acting on
those subsets. This subgroup is primitive when `2t + 1 ≤ |Δ|`, so the induced group
of `G` is primitive too (`Babai.cor_9_1_3_isPrimitive`). The returned bound
`2t + 1 ≤ |Δ|` follows from `rt < εm` and `ε ≤ 1/3`, as shown below.

*Strictness.*  This is the corollary with `>` in place of the paper's `≥`, which is what
Prop. 9.1.1 needs (a block of relative size exactly `1-ε` would not contradict
`ρ(Π) ≤ (1-ε)n`).  The paper's own proof gives it, once the case split is made at
`rt = εm` rather than at `rt/m > ε`: the contradiction of Eq. (50) needs only `εm ≤ rt`,
since then `εm/t ≤ r` and the chain runs as before; and in the remaining case `rt < εm` the
estimate `C(m-r,t) ≥ (1 - rt/m)·C(m,t) > (1-ε)·C(m,t)` is strict.  Equality really can
occur in `C(m-r,t) ≥ (1 - rt/m)·C(m,t)` (it is an equality for `r = 1`), so the case
split has to be the one above.  The paper's form is `Babai.cor_9_1_3` (below, after the
case `m ≤ 8`).

links.rationale: Intermediate step or helper for Proposition 9.1.1 (PDF p. 70) — Corollary 9.1.3.  *"Let `G ≤ Aut(J(m,t))` and `0 < ε ≤ 1/3`.  If `m!/|G| < (t/ε)^{εm/t}` then `G` acts as a primitive group on a subset of relative size `≥ (1 - ε)`."* (Version 2.5, lines 3953–3966.)
